Then build exactly per §4.11, one step at a time. Commit at each ✔ with `stage 02: <what>`.

Ground rules:
- The spec is the source of truth. If code has to deviate, update the spec and global spec in the same change, add a decision-log entry, and tell me. Never redefine global §7/§8 fields.
- Leakage (spec 02 §5): the few-shot examples in prompts must be invented, never taken from the three manifestos. The extraction LLM sees only manifesto units. V1–V3 checks run on every promise and every override.
- One code path for all parties: the layout profiles in config/manifestos.yaml describe typography only.
- All thresholds go in config/settings.yaml with the starting values from spec 02 §9 (OQ-1). No literals in code.
- Vendor the VANAVIL table from Open-Tamil 1.1 tamil/txt2unicode into src/ept/extract/vanavil_map.py. Keep the original copyright and GPL header. Add LICENSE (full GPL v3 text), THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, and license = "GPL-3.0-or-later" in pyproject.toml. pip install open-tamil fails on current Python, so take the files from the sdist tarball.
- API key: GEMINI_API_KEY is in .env. Never open, print, cat or commit .env. Load it through ept.config. Keep it out of logs, the cache key and run metadata. If it's missing, tell me.
- Tests run offline with EPT_LLM_MOCK=1. No test needs the key or Tesseract tam.
- Every step supports --term, --limit, --force, is idempotent, and refuses to touch frozen terms.

Mandatory pauses (stop and wait for me):
- After step 1: show me AIADMK pages 1 and 10 converted to Unicode Tamil, plus the per-page Tamil share and validity numbers.
- After step 2: report the calibration CER, how many TVK pages pass the OCR gate and how many need vision. If any need vision, do step 4 (_bulk + backend test) before transcribing them, because Gemini vision needs _bulk. Only pages Gemini still can't transcribe validly go to the Cowork fallback, and in that case tell me exactly what to run.
- After step 4: show me reports/backend_test_02.md and the model chosen by the rule. If no candidate reaches min_v1_pass, stop.
- After step 5 (--limit 20 per term): give me data/interim/spotcheck_02.csv (7–10 items, ≤3 per term, every column filled except verdict/note) and wait for my verdicts.
- Before freeze: the full-run spot-check has to be done and every acceptance criterion in §6 has to hold. Run `ept extract freeze` only after I say so.

Also stop and ask if: a manifesto has text the profiles can't read, the daily Gemini quota would stretch the full run past 2 days, or any leakage rule would have to bend.

Turn 38

What is the backend test and why does it need TVK manifesto units?

Claude's response

What the backend test is. Before running ~1,200 manifesto items through Gemini, we pick which free model does the extraction. The test runs the same 20 items through each candidate (gemini-3.8-flash and gemini-3.5-flash-lite) with the real extraction prompt and scores them automatically:

  • whether the output is valid JSON on the first try;
  • how often source_text is copied word for word from the manifesto (V1, the main criterion);
  • whether any number or name appears that isn't in the source (V2/V3);
  • promises per item, seconds per call, and rate-limit errors.

The model with the highest word-for-word copy rate wins, and a tie goes to the one with the larger daily quota. If neither copies correctly at least 90 % of the time, the build stops and asks you.

Why it includes TVK items. The test should look like the real job, and TVK is the hardest part of it. AIADMK is clean Tamil after the font conversion, and DMK is plain English. TVK text comes from OCR on a low-resolution scan, so it will have broken words and stray characters. That's exactly where a model is most likely to "clean up" the text instead of copying it, which would fail the word-for-word check. Or worse, it might fill gaps from what it already knows about the TVK manifesto, which is the leakage risk. Without TVK items, a model could ace the test on clean text and then quietly misbehave on the term that drives the projection. The mix (8 DMK, 6 AIADMK, 6 TVK) checks the three kinds of input separately.

One gap in the build order, which I found while answering this. The test needs TVK items, and those need TVK text. If some TVK pages fail OCR, their text has to come from Gemini vision, which needs the Gemini connection the test step builds. My Claude Code prompt said "do step 4 before transcribing", which would run the test before any TVK items exist. The clean fix is to split step 4 in two:

  • 4a: build the Gemini connection (_bulk) with offline tests, plus one live check call.
  • Vision transcription of any failed TVK pages, then cutting the TVK text into items.
  • 4b: run the backend test, now with real TVK items.

Vision transcription also needs a model before the test has chosen one. I'd use the stronger candidate, gemini-3.8-flash, under its own llm.models.vision setting, since reading images is a different job from extracting promises.

Should I make that change to the spec (v1.1, a short decision-log entry) and give you the corrected lines for the Claude Code prompt?

Ground rules:
- The spec is the source of truth. If code has to deviate, update the spec and global spec in the same change, add a decision-log entry, and tell me. Never redefine global §7/§8 fields.
- Leakage (spec 02 §5): the few-shot examples in prompts must be invented, never taken from the three manifestos. The extraction LLM sees only manifesto units. V1–V3 checks run on every promise and every override.
- One code path for all parties: the layout profiles in config/manifestos.yaml describe typography only.
- All thresholds go in config/settings.yaml with the starting values from spec 02 §9 (OQ-1). No literals in code.
- Vendor the VANAVIL table from Open-Tamil 1.1 tamil/txt2unicode into src/ept/extract/vanavil_map.py. Keep the original copyright and GPL header. Add LICENSE (full GPL v3 text), THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, and license = "GPL-3.0-or-later" in pyproject.toml. pip install open-tamil fails on current Python, so take the files from the sdist tarball.
- API key: GEMINI_API_KEY is in .env. Never open, print, cat or commit .env. Load it through ept.config. Keep it out of logs, the cache key and run metadata. If it's missing, tell me.
- Tests run offline with EPT_LLM_MOCK=1. No test needs the key or Tesseract tam.
- Every step supports --term, --limit, --force, is idempotent, and refuses to touch frozen terms.

Mandatory pauses (stop and wait for me):
- After step 1: show me AIADMK pages 1 and 10 converted to Unicode Tamil, plus the per-page Tamil share and validity numbers.
- After step 2: report the calibration CER, how many TVK pages pass the OCR gate and how many need vision.

- After step 6: show me reports/backend_test_02.md and the model chosen by the rule. If no candidate reaches min_v1_pass, stop.
- After step 7 (--limit 20 per term): give me data/interim/spotcheck_02.csv (7–10 items, ≤3 per term, every column filled except verdict/note) and wait for my verdicts.
- Before freeze: the full-run spot-check has to be done and every acceptance criterion in §6 has to hold. Run `ept extract freeze` only after I say so.

Also stop and ask if: a manifesto has text the profiles can't read, the daily Gemini quota would stretch the full run past 2 days, or any leakage rule would have to bend.

If a run will take more than a few minutes, write the exact command into docs/STATUS.md and I'll run it in my terminal.

At the end of the session: update docs/STATUS.md (checklist, session log with counts per term, next step), then commit.

I've read all five documents. Two things in the spec don't hold, so I'm stopping before writing any code. (.env doesn't exist yet. Details at the end.)

How I read the build order (spec 02 §4.11): 1. Licence files, settings, manifestos.yaml and the manifesto rows in documents. Then pages for DMK (text layer) and AIADMK (font map with the vendored VANAVIL table and overprint removal). Pause to show you AIADMK pages 1 and 10. 2. TVK: OCR, calibration on AIADMK pages rendered at 150 ppi, then the gate. Pause with the CER and the counts. Gated pages go to Gemini vision, which needs _bulk from step 4, so step 4 moves forward. Only pages Gemini can't transcribe validly go to Cowork. 3. units for all three terms, with the check that units plus furniture account for 100% of the characters. 4. _bulk and backend-test on a seeded sample of 8/6/6 units. The highest V1 pass rate wins, and I stop if no model reaches 0.90. 5. promises, checks, dedup and IDs on --limit 20 per term, then the report and spot-check. Pause for your verdicts. 6. Full run, a fresh spot-check, fixes, then freeze only when you say so.

Problem 1: the DMK facts in the spec don't match the PDF. I checked them against the real file: - Skipped numbers: 80, 136, 251 and 441. Item 18 is present. - Printed twice: only 166 and 252. The second "300." is item 42's text "Daily wage will be increased to Rs 300." wrapping onto a new line, so the cutter has to ignore it. - The 15-route rail sub-list belongs to item 442, not item 300. - Main items: 503 (505 − 4 skipped + 2 duplicates). With the 15 sub-list lines that makes 518, which matches the spec's total.

So the step 3 check "DMK has 505 main units" can't pass, and the coverage check can't map 80, 136, 251 and 441 because those numbers aren't printed. My proposal: - Change the check to 503 main units. - Record the four missing numbers as explained gaps ("number not printed"). - Fix the item 300 → 442 references in §2.1 and §4.5 S3. - Let a line count as a new item if its number equals the previous one or jumps ahead by at most a small amount (set in config), so the "Rs 300." line is rejected. - Log it as D-044.

Problem 2: there's a circular dependency. - The backend test needs 6 TVK units. - If TVK pages are gated, those units only exist after Gemini transcribes the pages. - Transcription needs a model, but the model is only chosen by the backend test.

Since the TVK scan is 150 ppi with colour bands, I expect most pages to be gated.

Not a spec issue: .env doesn't exist (I only checked that the file is there, not its contents). Steps 1–3 don't need it, but Gemini transcription and step 4 do.

"""`font_map` route (spec 02 §4.2, D-035): legacy-font Tamil spans -> Unicode.

Steps: read characters with their font and position; drop fake-bold overprint
copies; re-join characters into lines by position; convert each run of
legacy-font characters with the vendored VANAVIL table (so a word split across
spans is converted as one); keep other fonts as they are; NFC.

Overprint removal works per character, not per span: the copies of a bold line
are not always split into identical spans (e.g. "jä" x3 then "jäœ ehL"), so a
character is dropped when the same glyph was already kept within
`overprint_px` of its origin. This is the spec's rule applied at glyph level.
"""

• உரிய காலத்தில் கடனை திருப்பிச் செலுத்தும் விவசாயிகளுக்கு
முழு வட்டி மானியம் தொடர்ந்து வழங்கப்படும்.
கடந்த 5 ஆண்டுகளில் 20,787 கோடி ரூபாய் அளவிற்கு பயிர்க் கடன்
வழங்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. கடந்த திமுக ஆட்சியில் வழங்கப்பட்ட பயிர்க் கடன்
9,164 கோடி ரூபாய் தான்.
• விவசாய உற்பத்தியை அதிகரிக்கவும் விவசாயிகளின் நலன்களை
பாதுகாக்கவும் திட்டங்கள் செயல்படுத்தப்படும்.

படகுகளில் எந்திரம் பொருத்துவதற்கு மானியம் வழங்கப்படுகிறது.
மேலும், 580 மீனவர்கள் பயன் பெறும் வகையில் ஆழ்கடல் மீன் பிடிப்பதற்கு

• மீன் பதனப் பூங்காக்கள் அமைக்கும் நடவடிக்கைகள் தொடர்ந்து
எடுக்கப்படும்.
• கச்சத்தீவை மீட்டெடுத்து பாரம்பரிய மீன்பிடி இடங்களில் மீன்பிடி
உரிமையை நிலைநாட்டிட தொடர்ந்து நடவடிக்கை எடுக்கப்படும்.
• இலங்கை கடற்படையினரால் தமிழக மீனவர் கைது செய்யப்படும்
பிரச்சனைக்கு தீர்வு காணப்படும்.
• கடல் அரிப்பு உள்ள இடங்களில் தூண்டில் வளைவு அமைத்திட
நடவடிக்கை எடுக்கப்படும்.
• ஜல்லிக்கட்டு மீதான தடையை நீக்குவதற்கான நடவடிக்கைகள்
தொடர்ந்து எடுக்கப்படும்.
4. உழவர் பாதுகாப்புத் திட்டம் :
• வாழ்நாள் முழுவதும் பயனளிக்கக் கூடிய உழவர் பாதுகாப்புத் திட்டம்
தொடர்ந்து செயல்படுத்தப்படும்.
5. பேரிடர் இன்னல் குறைப்பு திட்டம் :
• கடலோர மாவட்டங்களில் புயல், வெள்ளம், சுனாமி போன்ற இயற்கை
சீற்றங்களால் ஏற்படும் பாதிப்புகளை தணிக்கும் கடலோர பேரிடர்
இன்னல்கள் குறைப்பு திட்டம் முழுமையாக நிறைவேற்றப்படும்.
பேரிடரிலிருந்து பாதுகாப்பு வழங்கும் வீடுகள் கட்டுதல், பாதுகாப்பு
மையங்கள் அமைத்தல், பாதுகாப்பு மையங்களுக்கான வழித்தடங்கள்

DMK has 29 English text-layer pages. The sidebar was removed on pages 1 and 3 (46 and 362 characters).

One decision for you (D-046a, logged as revisable)

Pages 26, 32 and 40 fall below 0.98 only because they print real English words in Latin fonts: "Cloud Computing", "Set-top Box", "Wi-Fi", "Amma Collateral Guarantee Fund", "Amma Banking Card", "Moped/Scooter". The spec's gate would send them to OCR, which would make good text worse. Instead I gate on the Tamil share of the converted legacy-font text, which measures conversion quality. The page-level share is still recorded, and these three pages will be listed in the report with the reason, which acceptance criterion 2 allows. OK to keep this?

Other changes in this commit (spec 02 v1.2)

  • D-045: the DMK correction you approved.
  • Overprint removal per glyph instead of per span. Fake-bold copies aren't split into identical spans, so equal-span matching would leave fragments.
  • rapidfuzz added for CER and dedup similarity.
  • New config keys: line_tol_px, space_gap_px, ocr_timeout_s, calibration_ppi, vision.max_unreadable (5) and max_number_jump (3). The [?] limit of 5 has no OQ-1 starting value, so I picked it; change it if you prefer another number.
  • Stage 01's parse now skips manifesto rows, so a --force re-parse can't overwrite them.

⏺ Bash — Replace invisible literal characters with escapes

.venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import re, pathlib
BS="\\"
for p in pathlib.Path("src/ept").rglob("*.py"):
    if p.name=="vanavil_map.py": continue
    s=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    def esc(ch):
        o=ord(ch)
        return f"{BS}u{o:04X}"
    # escape invisible / combining / format chars and Tamil block chars inside regex char classes only for listed files
    new=re.sub("[​-‍﻿஀்ௗ௿]", lambda m: esc(m.group()), s) if p.parent.name=="extract" else s
    if new!=s: p.write_text(new,encoding="utf-8"); print("fixed",p)
EOF

Step 2 is done and committed (733c5c8 stage 02: TVK OCR, calibration and gate). All 152 tests pass. This is the mandatory pause.

Results

  • Calibration CER: 0.030 on 5 AIADMK pages rendered at 150 ppi. Per page it ranges from 0.012 to 0.043, with mean confidence 84–92. That's below the 0.05 limit, so the gate decides page by page.
  • TVK gate: 79 of 96 pages pass and 17 go to vision:
  • 14 for confidence below 80 (pages 14, 24, 30, 43, 57, 58, 62, 66, 71, 84, plus the near-empty 1, 8, 35, 73, 96, partly overlapping);
  • 2 for validity below 0.98 (70, 86).
  • Near-empty pages: 8, 35 and 73 are the அறம் / பொருள் / இன்பம் divider pages (one word over a statue photo), 1 is the cover and 96 the back cover.
  • Page 1 is now TVK's first calibration page, because the reference is AIADMK, not TVK. Nothing to do here; just noting it.

Problem: pages that pass the gate are still noticeably wrong

  • Best page (p3, confidence 90): "முன்ணுர" for முன்னுரை, "பபாருள்" for பொருள், "நநெறிமுறை", "தீறமையற்ற", "குடூம்பம்", and "௦1" (Tamil digit zero) for 01.
  • Page 21 (passes, confidence 82): the white-on-red item headings, which are the promise titles, come out as nonsense, e.g. "அமமாத்து சமய மக்கருக்கும் புளரிருப் பயமா உநவித்டிதாசகை". The party initials print as "த.எவ.க." / "த.லவ.க.".

The gate doesn't catch this, because garbled words are often still orthographically valid, and the 0.030 calibration comes from clean black-on-white pages, which the spec already calls optimistic. Using this text means source_text (the verbatim span) carries OCR errors, and the headings that name each TVK promise are unreliable.

Sending all 96 pages to Gemini vision instead of 17 costs 79 extra calls, which is small against a free-tier daily quota. The OCR text stays as the cross-check for every page. The spec allows a revised threshold with a logged reason, so this is a config change (ocr_gate.max_cer 0.05 → 0.02), not a code change.

Before step 3

I've stopped: at this daily quota the full run would take far longer than the 2 days you set as the limit. Your decisions are needed on two things.

What happened

  • Quota: the 21st gemini-3.8-flash request today (smoke call, page 1, page 21, then this run) came back with a per-day quota error. So this model's free tier allows about 20 requests per day.
  • Accepted and committed: 14 pages (1–13 and 15) are in cb7eb04. Vision-vs-OCR CER is 0.015–0.07 on text pages. The exceptions are the cover (0.32) and the divider page 8 (1.0, because OCR found nothing there).
  • The 2 "failed" pages (14, 16) are false rejections. They print real English terms ("AR/VR", "Augmented Reality", "Hologram", "Mountain Biking", "Kayaking", "Nilgris Festival"), which pulls Tamil share down to 0.957–0.962. This is the same issue as AIADMK under D-046a. The retry with a note returned identical text, so 2 calls were wasted. Both responses are cached, so fixing the rule costs no new calls.

Call budget at about 20 requests a day

Work Calls (≈)
TVK vision, 80 pages left 80
Backend test (20 units ÷ 8, × 2 candidates) 6
Extraction (~1,300 units ÷ 8, plus single-unit retries) ~190
Dedup (one call per candidate pair, as specced) 50–150
Total ~330–430

At 20 a day that's 15–20 days on one model, or about 8–10 days if both Flash models have their own 20-a-day quota. The deadline is 2026-10-25, 12 days away. Even with bigger batches (25 units per call, 20 dedup pairs per call), it's still about 160 calls, roughly 4 days across both models.

Options

  1. Enable billing on the Gemini API project (paid tier). Rough cost at Flash pricing is a few US dollars for the whole stage, and the quota stops being a constraint. This conflicts with global §2 ("no paid API"), so only you can decide it. Code and specs barely change; it's a config change plus a log entry.
  2. Stay on the free tier and stretch it.
  3. Run vision on one Flash model and extraction on the other, since quotas are per model.
  4. Raise units_per_call to about 25, and batch dedup pairs about 20 per call.
  5. Even so, this is about 4+ days of quota-limited runs, and larger batches may lower the V1 pass rate.
  6. Kaggle fallback for extraction (D-037). This means real extra build work (a file handoff and an open model) and weaker Tamil quality.

To recommend between options 1 and 2, I'd need the per-day limit AI Studio shows for gemini-3.5-flash-lite. If you can see it, send it along.

"""`ept extract units` (spec 02 §4.4): cut each manifesto's page text into units.

One generic cutter, driven by the term's layout profile (D-040):
1. The term's pages are joined in order; every line keeps its page.
2. A line matching a furniture pattern is furniture (removed, counted).
3. A section heading (profile pattern, or a typographic heading line from `pages`)
   starts a new section. Consecutive heading lines form one heading block; the
   block's text is the `section` of the following units and is kept as the first
   lines of the next unit, so its words (and numbers) are seen by the LLM and every
   character is accounted for.
4. An item marker starts a unit: running numbers (DMK), bullets (AIADMK), per-section
   numbers (TVK). A number that equals the previous one or jumps ahead by at most
   `extract.max_number_jump` continues the sequence (D-045); a running number below
   the count opens a sub-list inside the current unit; a larger forward jump is text.

"""`ept extract dedup` (spec 02 §4.6, D-038, D-050): within-term duplicates, then IDs.

1. Every pair of promise texts in a term with token-set similarity >= `dedup.candidate_ratio`
   is a candidate.
2. Candidates go to the bulk model with `dedup_check.md`, `dedup.pairs_per_call` per call.
3. On "same", the later piece (document order) is dropped and logged in promise_dedup.csv;
   on "not same" both are kept (high-similarity "not same" pairs feed spot-check group e).
4. IDs only after dedup: `{term}-{seq:04d}`, contiguous in document order; `parent_group` =
   unit_id; `page` = page where `source_text` starts; `section` = `section_en`.
5. Coverage check for running-number manifestos: every printed main item maps to >= 1
   promise or to a logged reason; holes in the printed sequence are explained gaps.
"""

We can run the DMK-AIADMK part with Claude subagents as well, I have tokens to burn before today's 1.30 reset

Claude's response

I'd advise against switching DMK and AIADMK extraction to Claude. It wouldn't make things faster, and it creates consistency problems:

  • The Gemini path is ready and free. The full run is about 20 minutes and 45–55 calls, which fits in today's flash-lite quota plus the 12:30 reset. It costs no Claude tokens at all.
  • Claude would need new machinery. The extraction loop (batches, checks, single-unit retries, overrides) is wired to ept.llm with live calls. Claude subagents need a file handoff (export batches → agents → import, plus a second round for retries). That's roughly an hour of building and testing, then about 35 agent batches. It would finish later than the Gemini run.
  • One model for every term (§9.2 neutrality). If Claude extracts DMK and AIADMK, TVK should also be extracted by Claude later, and the backend test (which chose flash-lite on V1) no longer describes what was used. That means new decision entries and a re-run of the limit-20 check on the new model.

The best use of spare Claude tokens before your reset is the TVK transcription. It's already built and approved (D-057), and it runs alongside the Gemini extraction without touching the DMK/AIADMK path. It also removes about 4 days of daily Gemini runs from the TVK catch-up later.

Below is the plan for spec 03, set out in the §12.1 template, followed by the questions I need answered before the spec can be final.

Before we start: three things to tidy up

  • Stage 02 wrap-up isn't committed. CLAUDE.md, STATUS.md, 00-global-spec.md and two reports have changes, and there are two new backend-test run files. Should I commit them first as stage 02: wrap-up, so stage 03 starts from a clean tree?
  • Version labels don't match. The global spec header says v0.8, but STATUS says v0.7. STATUS also cites D-063, which isn't in the log (the log ends at D-062). I'll fix both when we close the spec.
  • Schedule: it's the end of Day 10, and stage 03 was planned for Day 11 with no buffer.

Plan for spec 03: Classification & decomposition (ept classify)

Purpose 1. Fill in the covariates on all 1,674 frozen promises: sector, promise_type, specificity, cost_band, union_dependent, continues_existing, headline and covariates_version. 2. Create the indicators rows. A specific promise gets one indicator, which is the promise itself (is_self). A vague promise gets 2–4. Every indicator carries search_queries for stage 04. 3. Answer Q-05 by fixing the rubrics: the sector list, the cost bands, and so on.

Inputs: data/frozen/promises_{term}.jsonl, read-only. The unit text from units.jsonl via parent_group, as context: STATUS says to use it, because some promises say "this scheme" and only the unit names it. Settings, and the bulk model gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Nothing from the evidence corpus.

Outputs: covariates written to the promises table in the database, the indicators table, prompts/classify_promises.md (with a version header), reports/classification_03.md (distributions by term, share of vague promises, check failures), spotcheck_03.csv, and a frozen snapshot (question 1).

How it works 1. The rubrics go into the spec and become enums in schema.py. §7 says spec 03 defines these values, so this doesn't redefine anything in §7. 2. One batched call handles roughly 20–25 promises at a time, about 80 calls in total. That fits easily in one day at 15 rpm and 500 per day. 3. Each item is checked against its own input: the IDs line up, every enum value is valid, the indicator count follows the rule (specific → exactly one, with is_self set; vague → 2–4), and the name/number check passes. An item that fails is retried on its own. That approach caught every misaligned batch in stage 02. 4. The party and term go nowhere in the prompt (neutrality, §9.2). The same prompt is used for all three terms. 5. Then the report, the spot-check, and the freeze. Every step supports --term, --limit and --force, and re-runs don't redo finished work.

Leakage section (rules 3 and 6, §9.1) - Covariates and indicators come from the manifesto text only. - An automatic check runs on every indicator and search query: any number, or any capitalised name, that isn't in the promise's text or its unit text fails the item. A few generic terms are allowed, such as "Tamil Nadu", "Union" and "Government". - Few-shot examples are invented. The same test as stage 02 applies: no 8-word overlap with any manifesto. - headline and continues_existing must not come from what the model remembers about which schemes later became famous or already existed (question 4). - There's no gold set yet, so gold leakage can't happen in this stage. I'll still note the rule in the spec.

Spot-check problem score (§12.4): in order, name/number check failures, items that needed a retry, vague promises with 4 indicators or a sector of other, headline = true, and outliers. At most 3 per term or per category. With three terms the global rule allows up to 9 items, so we don't need a D-054-style exception.

Acceptance criteria (draft): every promise has every covariate set, plus covariates_version. Every promise has at least one indicator, and the count rule holds. Name/number check failures: 0, or resolved through overrides. The few-shot overlap test passes. Re-running changes nothing. The limit-20 run and the spot-check are done.

Out of scope: retrieval and ranking (stage 04), judging, and any change to promise text or IDs.

Questions for you (each has my proposal, so "yes" is enough)

  1. Where do the covariates live? The frozen promise files are read-only, but §7 puts the covariates on promises. Indicator IDs will also become keys for retrievals and verdicts. Proposal: leave the promise snapshots untouched. Commit a separate data/frozen/classification_{term}.jsonl holding the covariates and indicators, frozen after sign-off under the same reasoning as D-039, and load the database from it.
  2. Sector list (Q-05). Proposal: 12 values that roughly follow TN department groupings, which may help stage 04 too: agriculture & fisheries · education · health · social welfare (women, children, elderly, disabled) · caste & minority welfare · employment & labour · industry, IT & MSME · infrastructure, transport & housing · rural & urban local government · water, environment & energy · governance, law & state rights · culture, Tamil language & religion · other. That's about 12 levels for 667 training rows in the Cox model. If you'd rather have fewer, I can merge some.
  3. promise_type and cost_band values.
  4. Types: new scheme · expansion of an existing scheme · cash or in-kind transfer/subsidy · infrastructure project · law or regulation · new institution or body · administrative/policy measure · advocacy to the Union (D-038a).
  5. Cost bands: a rough ordinal the LLM judges from the text: none/admin · low (one location or a targeted group) · medium (district-scale or a single scheme) · high (statewide entitlement or transfer). Is a judged band acceptable to you? The alternative is to fill it only when the manifesto states an amount, which would leave most rows unknown.
  6. headline and continues_existing: how strict, given leakage? Proposal: headline comes from structure and wording only (a promise in the preface or front matter, a highlighted or opening item, a statewide entitlement), with a cap of about 20–25 per term. The cap matters because §6.3 sends every headline promise to the Claude strong judge. continues_existing is true only when the text itself says so ("continue", "expand", "extend", or a named existing scheme). Should union_dependent use general constitutional knowledge (Union List subjects, Central approval)? That isn't outcome knowledge, so I propose yes.
  7. The vague/specific line. Proposal: specific means one checkable action with a clear object (amount or target optional), such as "provide Rs 1,000 per month to women heads of family". vague means a goal with no checkable action, such as "strengthen the fisheries sector". Item 1 of the cut order depends on this split, so I'll report the share of vague promises by term.
  8. Search queries: 2–4 English keyword queries per indicator, for every indicator including self ones. They contain no names or numbers beyond those in the promise and unit, under the check above. Or would you rather stage 04 own query generation? §6.1 lists "query expansion" as bulk work without saying which stage does it.
  9. One prompt or two? Proposal: one call does both classification and decomposition, which is cheaper and simpler. If the limit-20 run shows one task getting worse, I split them and log a decision.

Once you've answered, I'll draft specs/03-classification-decomposition.md and bring back anything still open before marking it final.

**Amendments 100–106 (from the page's table):**

- **100th (enforced 31 July 2015):** Exchanged certain enclave territories with Bangladesh and gave citizenship rights to enclave residents, following the Land Boundary Agreement. Amends the First Schedule.
- **101st (enforced 1 July 2017):** Introduced the Goods and Services Tax. Added Articles 246A, 269A, and 279A, deleted Article 268A, and amended several tax-related articles and the Seventh Schedule.
- **102nd (enforced 11 August 2018):** Gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (Articles 338B and 342A).
- **103rd (enforced 12 January 2019):** Provided up to 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections, through new clauses in Articles 15 and 16.
- **104th (enforced 25 January 2020):** Extended reserved seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies to 2030, and ended the reserved seats and nominations for the Anglo-Indian community.
- **105th (enforced 10 August 2021):** Restored states' power to identify Other Backward Classes, reversing a Supreme Court judgment of 11 May 2021 that had given that power only to the Centre (Articles 338B, 342A, and 366).
- **106th (enforced 28 September 2023):** Reserved one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, state assemblies, and the Delhi Legislative Assembly for 15 years (Articles 330A, 332A, 334A, and 239AA).

I've drafted spec 03 as specs/03-classification-decomposition.md, marked DRAFT v0.1. All your answers are folded in. Nothing is committed yet, and I haven't touched the global spec or the decision log; those change only once you approve.

Your Q6: yes, stage 04 needs the search queries. Retrieval is BM25 + dense (D-009), and the BM25 half works from keyword queries. search_queries is also a field on indicators in global §7. The queries come out of the same batched call that creates the indicators, so they add no LLM calls. Stage 04 has the heavier work anyway, so the queries stay in stage 03. Stage 04 can still add extra queries from corpus documents dated before each cutoff (the exception in leakage rule 6), but that's its job, not this stage's.

The constitution check (Q4): no amendment has been passed since the 106th (2023). The 131st Amendment Bill, on delimitation and women's reservation, was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April 2026. Two earlier changes fall inside our window: - GST (101st, in force July 2017): this came after the AIADMK-2016 election. To avoid using anything that happened after an election, the rubric goes by how the promise is worded: a promise about GST rates needs the Union side, while one about VAT or petrol tax stays a state power. - Backward-class lists (105th, August 2021): states hold this power in all three terms, so nothing changes.

What I added beyond what you approved, each with a check so the model can't fill it from memory: - continues_existing = true must quote the exact words from the manifesto that say it continues an existing scheme. - union_dependent must name its reason (advocacy, Union subject, Presidential assent, and so on). - Any number or capitalised name in an indicator or query must already appear in the promise; these failures go to the top of the spot-check. - The model writes indicators only for vague promises. For specific ones, the code makes the single indicator (the promise itself).

Four open questions before the spec is final (§9.4): 1. Headline mechanism. The model gives each promise a score of 0–3 from the text alone, and code keeps the top 25 per term. A term with fewer than 25 promises scoring 1 or more gets fewer than 25 headlines. Is that OK? 2. Where the audit fields live. The extra fields behind those checks (the quoted words, the reason, the headline score and rank) would sit only in the frozen snapshot and the report, not in the global §7 tables. Agreed? 3. Vague share. Should Claude Code stop and ask you if more than 50% of any term's promises come out vague? That share drives the stage 04/05 workload and the first item in the cut order. 4. Starting values. 20 promises per call, 2–4 indicators per vague promise, 2–4 queries of up to 12 words each. These can be revised after the limit-20 run.

Once you answer, I'll finalise it as v1.0, log D-064 to D-069, update the global spec to v0.9 and STATUS, and commit as stage 03: spec.

"""`ept extract promises` (spec 02 §4.5): units -> checked promise pieces.

Units go to the bulk model in fixed batches of `extract.units_per_call`, in document
order (deterministic batches -> stable cache keys). A unit whose output is missing or
holds a promise failing V1–V4 is retried alone, once; a piece that still fails is
logged to extract_failures_02.csv and not kept. Human fixes come from
config/promise_overrides.csv: a unit with override rows takes those rows as its
promises (checked like any other piece) instead of the model's promises.

Writes data/interim/manifestos/{term}/pieces.jsonl (accepted promise pieces, before
deduplication and IDs), and the term's rows of extract_dropped_02.csv and

"""`ept extract units` (spec 02 §4.4): cut each manifesto's page text into units.

One generic cutter, driven by the term's layout profile (D-040):
1. The term's pages are joined in order; every line keeps its page.
2. A line matching a furniture pattern is furniture (removed, counted).
3. A section heading (profile pattern, or a typographic heading line from `pages`)
   starts a new section. Consecutive heading lines form one heading block; the
   block's text is the `section` of the following units and is kept as the first
   lines of the next unit, so its words (and numbers) are seen by the LLM and every
   character is accounted for.

~/Projects/Election-Promise-Tracking/prompts/classify_promises.md
version: 1.0
purpose: classify each manifesto promise (covariates) and decompose vague promises into checkable indicators with search queries (spec 03 §4.2–§4.5, D-065–D-068). One prompt for every manifesto; the manifesto's text is data.

You classify promises taken from an election manifesto of an Indian state government, and you write checkable indicators and search queries for them.

Use ONLY the text given below: the front matter, each promise and the unit (manifesto item) it comes from. Do not use anything you know about any party, about Tamil Nadu, about what happened after the election, about which schemes already existed, or about which promises later became well known. The …

## Input
- `front_matter`: the manifesto's opening pages (title, preface), in the manifesto's language.
- `units`: manifesto items. Each has `unit` (a label), `section`, `unit_text` (original language; Tamil or English) and `promises`. Each promise has `id`, `text` (one English sentence), `source_text` (the span of the unit it comes from) and `source_lang`.

Return exactly one result for every promise `id`, with the same `id`.

"""Classification checks C1–C6 (spec 03 §4.4; leakage rules 3 and 6).

- C1 shape: exactly one result per input id, matched by id (never by position); enums and required
  fields valid (the pydantic output model enforces them; overrides are parsed through it too).
- C2 indicators: `specific` -> no `indicators`, 2–4 `search_queries`; `vague` -> 2–4 indicators, each
  with a text and 2–4 queries.
- C3 names and numbers, in every indicator text and every query: each digit group occurs in the promise
  `text`; each capitalised token that isn't a common word occurs in the promise `text`, its `source_text`
  (English units) or `section`. An indicator is a sentence, so its first token is exempt; a query is a
  keyword string, so none of its tokens is (stricter than the sentence rule: "Amma canteen" as a query
  would otherwise pass). Lower-case words are not checked.
- C4 cues: `continues_existing` ⇒ `continues_cue` is a verbatim span (after NFC, whitespace and quote
  normalisation, as V1 in stage 02) of the promise `text` or the unit text; false ⇒ empty cue.
  `union_dependent` ⇔ `union_basis` ≠ none.

"""`ept classify spotcheck` (spec 03 §4.7, global §12.4): the 7–10 most problematic items.

Problem groups, in priority order:

from ept.classify.headline import Candidate, assign, frontmatter_overlap, words


def test_ranking_order_and_tie_breaks():
    cands = [Candidate("T-0005", 2, "low", False), Candidate("T-0004", 2, "high", False),
             Candidate("T-0003", 2, "high", True), Candidate("T-0002", 3, "none", False),
             Candidate("T-0001", 2, "high", True), Candidate("T-0006", 1, "high", True)]
    out = assign(cands, cap=25)
    order = sorted((pid for pid in out if out[pid][1]), key=lambda p: out[p][1])

No term is near the 50 % vague limit. C3 failed on 6.5 % of first answers but on only 3.2 % after retries. That's under 5 % if your threshold counts what stays unresolved, so I didn't stop.

Problems I found, and prompt v1.1 changes to apply together with your verdicts: 1. Advocacy basis (13 retries): the model tags a promise as advocacy, then gives the subject (Union List, GST…) as the basis. Fix: tell it that advocacy promises always get basis advocacy, and that basis advocacy is only for advocacy promises. 2. Headline signal is 0 for all 62 promises, including "Waive all crop loans … small and marginal farmers". The model is under-scoring, and the full run would then pick almost no headline promises. Fix: state the statewide/large-group point more plainly, and add an invented example that scores 2. 3. Names: tell the model to copy names exactly as the promise text writes them, with no acronyms, and to describe in general words anything named only in the unit text.

Decisions I need from you: - Verdicts on the sheet, and OK (or changes) for prompt v1.1 above. - C3 and names that appear only in the unit text (item 2): I recommend keeping C3 strict. For Tamil units the code can't check an English spelling against Tamil script, so allowing unit-text names would only help DMK's English units, which isn't neutral. The cost is weaker search queries for "this scheme"-type promises.

Build clarifications, to log as D-071 after your review. Each is stricter than the spec or forced by it: - Promise and unit IDs contain the party and term (DMK-2021-0001), so the prompt gets batch-local aliases (P01…). Answers are matched back by alias, never by position. - C3 gives queries no exemption for the first word. Otherwise a query like "Amma canteen" would pass. - The C6 40-word limit applies only to indicators the model writes. A self indicator is the promise text, and 25 promises run 41–60 words, so they could never pass. - New config keys: min_query_words, goal_verbs, vague_stop_share. - The "appears in the front matter" test uses source_text, because the front matter is in the manifesto's language. - The stage 02 reload (load_frozen) now rewrites only stage 02 columns. Before this, ept extract dedup would have broken on the indicators foreign key and wiped the covariates.

Party names still reach the model as data: the front matter, and source texts like "DMK will…" or "on behalf of TVK". The global spec allows this. The prompt template itself names no party or term (tested).

Turn 76

Explain the impact of the choices 1 and 2 - advocacy and headline

Claude's response

Both changes only edit the prompt. The rules in spec §4.2 and §4.5 stay as they are; the prompt just states them more clearly.

1. Advocacy basis

What changes: the prompt will say that an advocacy promise always gets union_basis = advocacy, and that advocacy is used only for advocacy promises.

Effect on the stored data: small. Check C5 already enforces the first half, so no advocacy promise can be stored with the wrong basis today. The model just gets it wrong first time and the retry fixes it. The second half fixes cases C5 doesn't catch. In the limit-20 run, TVK-2026-0015 (an inter-state committee, typed institution) got union_dependent = true with basis advocacy. A state can form such a committee itself, so that should be false. union_dependent is a covariate in stage 07, so cases like this matter a little.

Effect on quota: the main reason for the change. 13 of 62 promises (21 %) needed a retry for this alone, at one extra call each. Across 1,674 promises that's roughly 350 extra calls on top of about 82 batch calls, close to the 500-a-day limit. Your stop rule is "more than one day's quota". With the fix, the full run should need about 100–130 calls.

What you lose: for an advocacy promise, union_basis can't also record what is asked for (a Union List subject, GST and so on). It's an audit field only, not used in modelling.

2. Headline signal

What changes: the prompt will spell out the "statewide entitlement or very large group" point (e.g. a benefit for all farmers, all women, every family card holder). It will also add an invented example that scores 2. The cap of 25 per term and the ranking stay as they are.

Why it matters: in the limit-20 run all 62 promises scored 0, including the crop-loan waiver for all small and marginal farmers. If the full run looks like that, very few promises get headline = true, which has three effects: - Stage 05: headline promises are one of the routes to the Claude strong judge (global §6.3). With almost none, that route covers almost nothing. - Stage 07: headline is a covariate. If it's almost always false, it carries no information. - Stage 08: the website's headline filter would be close to empty.

With the change I'd expect each term to fill or come close to its 25. That means up to 75 promises in total going to the strong judge, which is the load the spec planned for.

Risks: - Model knowledge: the model's background knowledge could tilt which promises get points, for example favouring promises that later became famous. The prompt forbids this and the criteria are textual, but nothing checks it mechanically. This is already a known limitation in spec §5 and will go in the whitepaper. The headline boundary is on the spot-check (group d). - Front-matter asymmetry (not caused by v1.1, but it will show more): the third point is "named in the front matter". DMK's front matter is just its title, "DMK ELECTION MANIFESTO 2021". AIADMK has about one page and TVK about 11,000 characters of preface. So DMK promises can never earn that point. Within-term rankings are unaffected, because each term has its own cap of 25. But a signal of 2 doesn't mean the same thing across terms, which matters if stage 07 uses the signal rather than the flag. If you want, I can log this as a known limitation. The alternative is to drop the front-matter point for all terms, which would be a spec change.

Cost of v1.1 overall

Changing the version number gives every prompt a new cache key, so the 18 limit-20 calls are discarded and everything is re-asked. Before the full run, I'd do another limit-20 run (about 4–8 calls) to confirm the C5 retries are gone and headline signals appear.

Recommendation: approve both. Log the front-matter asymmetry as a known limitation and keep the point, since the rankings within each term are what drive the headline flag.

What the global spec already fixes for stage 04

  • Commands and output: ept index and ept retrieve write the retrievals table, which §7 already defines (indicator_id, chunk_id, rank, scores, cutoff_date, run_id). No new fields go into §7.

  • Cutoff rule (§9.1): a chunk is kept only if period_end(doc_date, date_precision) is on or before the cutoff. Undated chunks are left out of every cutoff run. This needs a unit test.
  • Must decide or report: Q-06 (which embedding model, and how many chunks per judgment). §13 also asks for a report of how much evidence exists at each landmark.

Plan for spec 04 (§12.1 template)

  1. Purpose: for each indicator and each cutoff, store the top k chunks. Stage 05 judges from these.
  2. Inputs: chunks and documents (read-only), the frozen classification snapshots, and a new retrieve: block in settings.yaml. Not used: manifesto units, gold labels, verdicts, the web.
  3. Outputs:
  4. Code in src/ept/retrieve/ (index, bm25, dense, fuse, cutoff, run, report, spotcheck).
  5. Embeddings in data/processed/. They can be rebuilt, so they aren't committed.
  6. Rows in retrievals.
  7. reports/retrieval_04.md/json, spotcheck_04.csv, run metadata and tests.
  8. Behaviour:
  9. Index once: ept index embeds every chunk a single time. Each embedding depends only on its own chunk, so one index serves every cutoff.
  10. Eligible chunks: for each term and cutoff, apply the §9.1 filter, plus the term window from Q2 below.
  11. BM25 per cutoff: build BM25 on the eligible chunks only. Otherwise the word statistics would come partly from documents after the cutoff. That's the strict reading of leakage rule 2, and it costs only seconds per run.
  12. Embedding search: exact search with numpy inside the eligible set, instead of FAISS. 60k vectors is small, the search is exact and filtering is simple. This needs a logged deviation from §11.
  13. Combining: rank-based fusion (RRF) of the BM25 result for each query with the embedding result. scores stores both ranks and raw scores.
  14. Spread: at most 2 chunks from any one document.
  15. Same settings for every term.
  16. Report:
    • Evidence available per term and cutoff, by document type and date source.
    • Indicators with no BM25 hit, and how much BM25 and embedding search agree.
    • The document-type mix of what was retrieved.
    • How the 43 promises with generic override queries fare.
  17. Spot-check problem score:
  18. (a) BM25 and embedding top-k don't overlap at all;
  19. (b) both methods score low;
  20. (c) one of the 43 generic-query promises;
  21. (d) a headline promise;
  22. (e) a top chunk dated close to the cutoff or by Wayback.
  23. At most 3 items per term or group, and one per promise.
  24. The sheet shows the indicator, its queries and the top 5 chunks (title, type, date, a short snippet around the match). The question per item is "is at least one of these relevant?", which keeps each item under 2 minutes.
  25. Leakage section:
  26. Rule 2: the cutoff filter, BM25 built per cutoff, undated chunks excluded.
  27. Rule 6: no expansion unless Q5 allows it.
  28. Rule 1: this stage decides what the judge will see.
  29. Rule 4: there is no gold set yet.
  30. Neutrality.
  31. Acceptance criteria and tests:
  32. Check the database for any cutoff violation.
  33. Test the exact boundaries; for example, a document dated only to "2021" is not eligible for a 2021-06-30 cutoff.
  34. Results come out the same on every run, and re-runs skip finished work.
  35. Tests run offline with a mock embedding model.
  36. Out of scope: judging, Tamil evidence, any new crawling, LLM-based reranking.

Questions before I draft (my recommendation first)

  • Q1 – Which cutoffs to retrieve?
  • Recommendation: full term for all three terms; AIADMK and DMK at months 6, 12, 24, 36 and 48; TVK at its current month (5, as of the corpus snapshot of 2026-10-09).
  • Retrieval runs locally and is cheap. The free-tier quota only matters in stage 05, which can choose which of these to actually judge.
  • Also add month 5 for AIADMK and DMK, so TVK can be compared at the same month (RQ3)?
  • Q2 – Date window for a full-term run (cutoff_date null)?
  • The lower bound would be sworn_in, since realisation can't come before it (§9.1).
  • For the upper bound, a hard stop at term_end drops many AIADMK policy notes and CAG reports, because their Wayback dates come months or years late. Allowing all later documents would give AIADMK five or more years of hindsight against DMK's five months, which breaks symmetry.
  • Recommendation: term_end plus the same fixed grace for every term, about 5 months (all DMK can have), plus undated chunks (§9.3 allows them in full-term runs only).
  • Q3 – Chunks per judgment (Q-06)?
  • Recommendation: k = 8 per indicator, the same 8 for the Gemini judge and the Claude judge, so the stage 06 comparison between them is fair.
  • For the Claude judge, 20 tasks × 8 chunks is about 90k tokens per batch. Batch size is Q-07 in stage 05.
  • Q4 – Embedding model?
  • Recommendation: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, run locally on the Mac. It reads up to 512 tokens, which fits most 300–500-word chunks; the end of the longest ones gets cut.
  • Alternatives:
    • bge-base: better, about 3× slower.
    • all-MiniLM: stops at 256 tokens, so it would cut half of most chunks.
    • Gemini embeddings: network-bound, and the results depend on the API rather than a local model.
  • This means installing torch and sentence-transformers and downloading the model from Hugging Face. If Claude Code's network can't reach Hugging Face, you'd run the download yourself.
  • Q5 – Query expansion?
  • Recommendation: none for now (no LLM calls, no quota). Revisit only if the limit-20 spot-check shows misses concentrated in the 43 generic-query promises.
  • The fallback would be expansion from top results within the eligible chunks only. Those are all dated before the cutoff, so it satisfies rule 6 automatically.
  • Q6 – Reserve places for GOs?
  • The realisation date is the first GO, launch or law, but policy notes and budget speeches that describe a scheme may outrank the original GO.
  • Recommendation: reserve up to 2 of the 8 places for GOs, if any GO ranks within the top 50 after fusion. The same rule applies to every term. Or leave the ranking as it is?

Q1: the website can still show TVK at any month

The cutoffs don't limit what the website can show. Stage 07 fits survival curves on each promise's realisation date, and a survival curve is continuous: it gives P(realised by month t) for any t, month by month. So the TVK page can show a projected curve over the whole term, with uncertainty bands.

The landmark cutoffs do two other jobs: - Validation: the backtest checks the model's accuracy at those months. Between landmarks, the curve is the model's interpolation and isn't separately validated. The whitepaper would say so. - Starting point: TVK's month-5 position is the observed starting point the projection builds on.

I'll add month 5 for AIADMK and DMK as well (you didn't say either way). It's cheap, and it lets the backtest start from the same point we have for TVK. So the cutoffs are months 5, 6, 12, 24, 36 and 48, plus full term, for AIADMK and DMK, and month 5 plus full term for TVK.

Q2: bounding to the term loses a lot of AIADMK evidence

Your call stands, but you should see what it costs first: - Of the 8,609 policy-note chunks for AIADMK's fiscal years (2016-17 to 2020-21), 1,521 are dated after 2021-05-06. Their date is the first Wayback capture, an upper bound, not the issue date. - Another 1,567 undated chunks belong to those same AIADMK years. - So a strict date bound drops about 3,100 chunks of AIADMK-era government text from AIADMK's full-term run. DMK loses little, because its documents mostly have listing or © dates. - TVK's window holds only 1,507 chunks in total.

Two options for full-term runs only: - A (strict): period_end(doc_date) between sworn_in and term_end. Undated chunks are left out. - B (dated by term, or by fiscal year): the A rule, plus any chunk dated after the term or undated whose fiscal_year is one of that term's fiscal years. The years would be fixed in config: - AIADMK: 2016-17 to 2020-21. - DMK: 2021-22 to 2025-26. - TVK: 2026-27 onward. - CAG reports are left out of the fiscal-year rule. Audits are written after the fact, and DMK has no matching later audits yet, so including them would break symmetry.

Both options keep the result bound to the term. B goes by the period a document was written for, not by when Wayback first saw it. Cutoff runs stay strictly by doc_date either way, so nothing written later can appear at a landmark.

I recommend B. Without it, AIADMK's full-term verdicts, which are the backtest's ground truth, would be judged on noticeably thinner evidence than DMK's.

Q3: k tuned for Claude

  • At 392 words per chunk on average (about 520 tokens), k = 5 comes to roughly 3k tokens per task. A batch of 20 is then about 60k tokens, against about 95k at k = 8.
  • I'd keep the same 5 chunks for the Gemini judge, so the stage 06 comparison between the two judges stays fair.
  • Stage 05 can save more by grouping a promise's indicators into one task and sending shared chunks only once.
  • The Claude judging can only start once stage 04 is built and stage 05 can export batches (Day 17 on the current schedule), so the fresh weekly limit is what it will use.

Q6: yes, a GO that's the only source still ranks 1

The reserved places never push anything down: - The list is first ranked by the fused score. - If it holds fewer than 2 GOs, the lowest non-GO is swapped for the best GO from the top 50. - The list is then re-sorted by score.

So a GO that is the only matching source ranks first on its own score.

The real risk is the search not finding the GO at all: - Different wording: GOs use official, department wording ("Enhancement of payment of ex-gratia to the families of the Para Military Force Personnel…") rather than manifesto wording. - OCR errors: the sample I pulled has "Personne!", "arinual" and "G.0.", which break exact keyword matches.

Embedding search copes better with both, and a GO's title is its one-sentence summary (the "Abstract"). So I propose adding the document title to every chunk before BM25 and embedding search. Then each chunk of a GO carries its subject line, not only the first one. Stored chunk text stays unchanged.

One limitation remains: if several GOs touch a promise, the search may find a later amending GO rather than the original. The judge would see the reference to the original ("Read: G.O. Ms. No. …") but couldn't cite it. I'll record this as a known limitation.

Before I draft spec 04 v0.1, please confirm

  1. Q2: option A or B?
  2. k = 5, with up to 2 places for GOs?
  3. Add the document title to each chunk for searching?

You're right. A government out of office can't write policy notes, so those out-of-term dates come from how they were dated, not from what the documents are. The date stored for them is the first Wayback capture, which only tells us the file existed by then. The data supports a better upper bound.

What the data shows

  • The fiscal year is reliable. It comes from the official file name and title (hedu_e_pn_2018_19.pdf, "Policy Note of Higher Education Department – 2018-2019"), not from a guess.
  • Documents with an independent date always fall inside their fiscal year:
  • All 165 policy notes with a © year have the fiscal year's first year (a 2019-20 note says © 2019).
  • All 14 budget speeches with a day date fall on or before their fiscal year's end.
  • None of the 179 breaks the rule.
  • The reason is structural. A policy note goes with that year's request for funds, so it has to be tabled before the fiscal year ends. Even in election years, notes come out after the new government takes office (2016-17 in July 2016, 2021-22 in Aug–Sep 2021), still within the year. So the end of the fiscal year (31 March) is a guaranteed upper bound.

What I'd do

Rule: a document's "available by" date = the earlier of its stored date's period end and the end of its fiscal year. This applies only to policy notes, performance budgets and budget speeches, whose fiscal year is the year they were written for.

Everything else keeps its stored date: - CAG reports: their fiscal year is the period audited; the report itself comes years later. - GOs: they already have listing dates. - Governor's addresses: how their fiscal year maps to a date is unclear. - Scheme pages: they have no fiscal year.

What this fixes: - 87 policy notes and 16 performance budgets with Wayback dates after their fiscal year now get the tighter date. - 89 undated documents (70 policy notes, 17 performance budgets, 2 budget speeches) get a date and become usable at cutoffs. - So "bound to the term duration" (your Q2, option A) works without any special fiscal-year exception, because these notes now fall inside their own term. - It also helps cutoff runs: AIADMK's notes become visible at the landmarks where they actually existed. Before, the late Wayback date hid them until years later. - The date never moves earlier than the date the document actually existed, so there's no leak.

Where it goes: - One function, ept.dates.available_by(...). Stage 04 uses it for the cutoff and term filters; stage 05 uses it for the check that a realisation date is no later than the latest cited chunk's date. - Stored stage 01 dates stay unchanged, so §7 and the corpus aren't touched. - It needs a wording change to global spec §9.1/§9.3 (the cutoff rule currently names period_end(doc_date) directly) and a decision-log entry, both made with spec 04.

Two things I considered and rejected: - Re-dating the documents in stage 01: that's outside this stage and would need a new date-source value in §7. - A tighter bound of 31 December of the first year, which the © years suggest: it's not guaranteed the way the 31 March deadline is.

Small remaining risk: D-018 keeps the latest version of a file at a URL. If a department re-uploaded an edited note after its fiscal year, we'd see the edits. Policy notes are tabled once, so I'd log this as a known limitation.

  3. Add the document title to each chunk for searching?

What I'd propose

1. Spot-checks stop blocking the pipeline. Only irreversible steps wait for them. - Steps that would wait: freezing a term, spending Claude quota on judging, and closing a stage as "done". - Everything else carries on while a check is pending. - For stage 04 that's everything, because retrievals aren't frozen and a re-run takes minutes. So Claude Code would do the full run, prepare the check, and move on to spec 05 the same day. If you later mark something wrong, the fix is a cheap re-run.

2. One human check per stage instead of two. - The 20-item trial run stays, as an automatic test for crashes and obvious errors. - You review only the full run. - For stage 04, that halves your load (the spec currently asks for two checks). - Exception, stage 05: I'd keep one short check before the Claude-judge batches. A bad judge prompt there burns your week's Claude limit, which can't be recovered.

3. Checks you can do in 2-minute slots on your phone. - Claude Code writes the sheet as now. - In a session like this one, I publish it as a private page with one item per screen: the question, the evidence with the matching words highlighted, and ok / wrong / unsure buttons with an optional note. - Your taps are saved as you go, so 7 items can be spread over a day. - I then write your verdicts back into the CSV in your project folder. - Each item is built to be a yes/no you can answer in about a minute.

4. Seven items, not ten. The global rule allows 7–10. Stopping at the minimum saves a few minutes per check without changing the rule.

One option I'd avoid as a default: having a separate Claude pre-fill the verdicts so you only confirm them. It's faster, but you'd tend to agree with whatever it suggested, so it stops being an independent human check. It's also unsafe wherever the model's own knowledge could leak into a verdict (stages 05–06). For stage 04 relevance checks it would be acceptable if you're desperate.

Labelling doesn't depend on any model output; it has to be done blind to the verdicts anyway. So it can start now, in parallel, a few promises at a time on the same phone page. 200 - **D-001 · 2026-10-05 · Only ruling parties are analysed.** Only a governing party can fulfil a manifesto.
201 - **D-002 · 2026-10-05 · No scandal, favourability or composite party scores.** They hide subjective weights, carry defamation risk and invite bias accusations.

def fy_bounded(doc_type: str, title: Optional[str], fy_bound) -> bool:
    """Policy notes, budget speeches, and `other` documents whose title starts with a listed prefix."""
    if doc_type in fy_bound.doc_types:
        return True
    prefixes = fy_bound.title_prefixes.get(doc_type) or []
    t = (title or "").strip().lower()
    return any(t.startswith(p.lower()) for p in prefixes)

I've drafted the gold-set part of spec 06, drawn the ordered sample and published the labelling page. Nothing is labelled yet; it's waiting for your approval.

Spec. specs/06-evaluation.md is DRAFT v0.1 and covers Part 1 (the gold set) only; Part 2 is a stub. It uses your four choices and the defaults I listed: - Each label is the status at the end of the term (TVK: 10 Oct 2026). Landmark results are worked out from the realisation date, so one label covers every landmark. - You label in order and never skip. Use unverifiable or tick Unsure instead. - The page shows no model output. Claude doesn't research, suggest or pre-fill anything. - Q-08: you re-label 8 promises blind on the 24th or 25th to check your own consistency.

Proposed decisions D-081–D-085 are in §G12. They aren't in the log yet.

Sample. data/gold/gold_sample.csv has 78 promises in a fixed order (seed ept-gold-2026-10-20). - Positions 1–40 are the minimum: AIADMK 16 specific + 4 vague, DMK 17 specific + 3 vague, 4 headline promises, spread over 22 term-sector combinations. - DMK vague promises are oversampled to 15 % (they're 6.3 % of DMK's promises), so Part 2 weights them back down. - At most one promise comes from each manifesto item. - Re-running data/gold/draw_gold.py gives the same list.

Labelling page (the card above). One promise per screen, with: - the English text, the Tamil original and the full manifesto item; - the seven status buttons, and a date with day/month/year precision for fulfilled/partial/diluted; - up to 8 corpus passages per promise from plain keyword matching on the promise's own words, with matched words highlighted (no model output involved); - a search over all 9,186 document titles, and a field for web URLs.

in_corpus is set automatically from what you cite, and a timer turns amber at 6 minutes. Every change is saved as you go, and the page reopens at the next unlabelled promise. I tested it at phone width with a stand-in for the real storage: a full save worked and validation caught a missing status. On the live page I could only confirm that storage is reachable and empty. I haven't saved anything through it.

Four things to confirm (OQ-G1–G4): 1. TVK position. I put the 8 TVK promises at positions 41–48, right after the minimum. At 71–78, the literal "end of the order", you'd almost never reach them. Is that OK? 2. "Urge the Union" promises. If the state took the formal step (resolution, letter, GO), it counts as fulfilled. If the promise is an outcome only someone else can deliver, it's blocked_external when the state acted and it didn't happen. Stage 05 would have to use the same reading. 3. Evidence format. Several sources per label, separated by ;, plus a doc:<id> form for documents found by title search. This changes only the format of §7's evidence field, not the schema. 4. Stopping point. Labelling stops at the end of 24 Oct (IST).

Turn 88

I am having trouble classifying promises which don’t have a set end goal but measures have been taken in that direction. for now I’m choosing Partial and adding notes to such promises, but I don’t think that’s the best way to handle them. I can’t think of a way to quantify how well that promise has been fulfilled. What do you suggest?

Claude's response

I'd stop using Partial for these and add one rule to §G4. Partial means "some listed parts done, others not", and these promises have no list of parts. Partial plus a note also mixes them in with real Partials, and the judge can't learn a rule that only lives in your notes.

You don't have to measure how far a promise got. The primary survival event (E1) treats fulfilled, partial and diluted the same: it only asks whether there was a qualifying official step and when. So for these promises, the two things that matter are whether a step happened and when the first one happened. The status enum only says what kind of delivery happened, never how much.

Proposed rule: directional promises. This covers promises that commit only to effort or direction ("promote", "encourage", "strengthen", "take steps towards"), with no amount, target or list of parts: - Fulfilled: the state took at least one dedicated official measure during the term: a new GO, scheme, programme or law whose subject is what the promise is about. The realisation date is the date of the first such measure. - In progress: the only step is preparatory, such as a committee, a draft policy or a tender, with nothing in operation. - Not started: only mentions in a policy note or budget speech, or the same activity carrying on with no new step. - Partial and diluted don't apply, because there's nothing defined to fall short of. - Add a [directional] tag in the note, so Part 2 can report accuracy with and without these promises. If they turn out shaky, that shows up as a measured limitation rather than noise.

For example, take an invented promise, "Promote rooftop rainwater harvesting." A GO in year 2 that makes it mandatory for new buildings means fulfilled, dated to that GO. A paragraph in a policy note saying the department "encourages" it is not enough.

This rule is generous: one real measure makes it fulfilled. The other options are worse, though. A new status would mean changing global §8, and both judges and stage 07 would have to handle it. A "degree" score would be judgment you can't make the same way twice, and stage 05 would need to copy it.

What this needs from you: 1. Say yes or adjust the rule. I'll add it to spec 06 §G4 and the page's Rules sheet, and add a "Directional" chip next to Unsure. Stage 05's judge then uses the same written rule, taken from the spec and not from your labels. This turn I can't reach your Mac, so the spec edit happens once it's linked again. The page I can update from here. 2. Re-check the ones you've already marked Partial for this reason. If you want, I can list the positions where you chose Partial and wrote a note. I'd show only the position numbers, with no opinion on any of them, and you re-apply the rule yourself.

One check while you label: if a directional promise also names a concrete part ("promote organic farming and set up 100 certification centres"), it isn't purely directional. Label it normally, and Partial is right if only some of it was done.

"""`ept retrieve spotcheck` (spec 04 §4.10, global §12.4): the 7–10 most problematic indicator × cutoff items.

Problem groups, in priority order:
  a. method disagreement + weak: BM25 top k and dense top k share no chunk, and the top-1 dense cosine is in
     the term's bottom quartile;
  b. weakest evidence on a full-term run (lowest top-1 rrf, then cosine);
  c. the generic-query override promises (config/classify_overrides.csv), lowest top-1 cosine;
  d. headline promises, lowest top-1 cosine;
  e. date-sensitive: a selected chunk whose available_by comes from the fiscal-year bound, or lies within
     `near_cutoff_days` before the run's upper bound;
  f. fill: a GO-place chunk that displaced a higher-ranked chunk.
At most `per_term` per term and `per_group` per group, one item per promise; within a group the terms take
turns (best item of each term first). A sheet that already holds verdicts is archived, never overwritten.

The difference is only in performance budgets and doesn't affect the rule. - Title vs stored fiscal year: 3 performance budgets have a fiscal year in the title one year earlier than the stored one (the URL agrees with the stored one). That only makes their bound later, so it can't leak. - Eligible sets: none is empty. They range from 1,010 chunks (AIADMK month 5) to 31,829 (DMK full term). - Index: bge-small-en-v1.5 pinned at 5c38ec7c… and credited in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. 500 chunks took 6.8 s, so I ran the full index here: 60,259 chunks in 14 min. - Limit-20 smoke test: leakage line 0, 5 rows per indicator, at most 2 chunks per document, GO rule met, eligible counts rise at each landmark. - Full run: 8,433 tasks and 42,165 rows in 217 s. Leakage line 0, 0 undated chunks, and a second run writes nothing. - Snapshots: the frozen promise and classification files are byte-identical. The stage writes only to retrievals. - Stage 05 sizing: AIADMK 2,695 tasks, DMK 4,970, TVK 768. Each task's 5 chunks plus titles come to about 2,150 words, or ~2,860 tokens (spec estimated 2.6k), before the prompt.

Build changes, logged as D-081 - The run fingerprint also covers the code that shapes the rows, so a code fix starts a new run instead of resuming stale rows. - The cutoff guard's "corpus snapshot" is also capped at the latest fetch date. Taken literally, the spec's fallback gives 2027-03-31, a future date. - Stage 03's freeze helper had a regex that hung once settings.yaml grew the new retrieve: block; I fixed it and its behaviour is unchanged. - A small run-metadata bug: a resume that writes nothing overwrites the timing records. The rows are unaffected; I restored the records from the logs. The fix waits for stage close, because changing that code changes the fingerprint and would orphan the complete run.

Decisions for you (non-blocking) 1. Sheet coverage: following the spec's spread rule, the sheet caps at 9 items (3 per term), and groups a–c fill all of them. Headline, date-sensitive and GO-place items get none. That includes the date check D-077 relies on for chunks dated only by their fiscal year. Keep it as drawn, or swap some group c items for date-sensitive ones? 2. TVK month 5 recall (not a leak): 2,407 chunks of 2026-27 policy notes, budget speeches and performance budgets are dated only by © 2026 or their fiscal-year end. So none is eligible at the 2026-10-10 cutoff, and TVK has only 1,507 eligible chunks. These documents were probably tabled in mid-2026, but no stored date shows it. Changing this needs a decision from you.

I've made both changes, re-run the full retrieval, and redrawn the sheet. All 283 tests pass, and it's committed as 075e164.

TVK documents: a document now counts as available no later than the day we downloaded it, since it must have existed by then. This is your "released while in power" rule in a form that can't leak (D-082). - No dates invented: documents with no date at all stay excluded. Otherwise old undated CAG reports would suddenly count as TVK-era evidence. - Interim budgets kept out. The corpus has two kinds of 2026-27 budget documents: the outgoing government's interim budget (Feb 2026) and TVK's own documents. The undated Agriculture Interim Budget Speech 2026-27 belongs to the outgoing government, so I excluded titles containing "interim budget". I added this exception myself because your rule assumes the documents are TVK's; say if you'd rather drop it. - TVK month 5: 61 documents from 2026-27 (55 policy notes, 5 performance budgets, TVK's agriculture budget speech), all downloaded on 2026-10-07/08, are now available. Eligible chunks went from 1,507 to 3,895. - Are they TVK's? 45 of the 61 name Vijay or mention months after May 2026. The other 16 follow the election-year pattern from 2016 and 2021, where the new government tables that year's policy notes. - AIADMK and DMK are unchanged: all their documents were downloaded after their terms ended, and the new run gives them exactly the same retrievals as before. - TVK quality: median top-1 similarity went from 0.645 to 0.696. TVK's evidence is now 66% policy notes and 24% GOs.

Spot-check sheet: one place per term is now kept for a date check (group e) (D-083). The sheet is still 9 items: - AIADMK: a, b, e (its c item swapped). - TVK: a, c, e (one of its c items swapped). - DMK: a, b, e. DMK had no c item, so its second b was swapped instead.

TVK's date item checks one of the policy notes now dated by its download day (2026-10-08).

New run retrieve-20261020T191347Z, leakage check 0. Global spec is now v0.12, spec 04 v1.2, and STATUS is updated. The sheet is ready at data/interim/spotcheck_04.csv, with the item pages in data/interim/spotcheck_04/.

# Decision log

One line per settled decision: ID · date · decision · reason. Settled decisions are not reopened without a new entry.

- **D-001 · 2026-10-05 · Only ruling parties are analysed.** Only a governing party can fulfil a manifesto.
- **D-002 · 2026-10-05 · No scandal, favourability or composite party scores.** They hide subjective weights, carry defamation risk and invite bias accusations.
- **D-003 · 2026-10-06 · Terms:** DMK 2021–26 (training), AIADMK 2016–21 (backtest target), TVK 2026– (projection). AIADMK 2011–16 only if time allows.
- **D-004 · 2026-10-06 · Terms treated as independent.** A stated assumption in the whitepaper.
- **D-005 · 2026-10-06 · Reverse backtest first** (train DMK-2021 → test AIADMK-2016), for recency. Forward backtest added later; the reverse one is the primary and is never cut.
- **D-006 · 2026-10-06 · Vague promises are decomposed into checkable indicators.**
- **D-007 · 2026-10-06 · The hand-labelled gold set is test-only,** never used for training or prompts.

B. Proposals I'll write in unless you object

  1. Carry-forward across cutoffs. Each cutoff's verdict is stored exactly as judged.
  2. The derived state at month m is "realised" if any run at a cutoff ≤ m has a checked realisation date ≤ m. This doesn't leak, because evidence available at an earlier cutoff is still available at m.
  3. The full-term realisation date = the earliest checked date across all of that term's runs. This fixes cases where a later cutoff's top 5 pushes out the original GO.
  4. When verdicts contradict each other across cutoffs, the item is flagged.
  5. Gold labels are never "human" final verdicts. Otherwise they would enter the DMK training fit and make stage 06 circular (spec 06 §G5.6). Human verdicts come only from spot-check fixes.
  6. Indicator-level verdicts get an indicator_verdicts table, added to global §7. Stages 06 to 08 read it, and CLAUDE.md keeps shared schema in §7 only.

    • A small memory probe: about 40 tasks with the chunks blanked out, a few bulk calls. It measures how often the model claims a promise was realised with no evidence; the result is reported in stage 06.

  8. One human spot-check, on the full bulk run, done before any strong-judge batch (D-080 allows this earlier check). The problem score, in order:

    • (a) items still failing a check after the retry;
    • (b) a realisation date close to a cutoff, or failing the date rule;
    • (c) realised verdicts on headline promises with low confidence;
    • (d) verdicts that contradict each other across cutoffs;
    • (e) a realisation verdict resting only on a budget speech or policy note, which may break the "announcements don't count" rule.

    At most 3 items per term and per group, as in earlier stages. 14. Timing. - Spec today, then build and the limit-20 smoke test. - Bulk run over the Pacific days of 22–23 October. - Strong judge on 23–24 October.

I've drafted specs/05-judgment.md (v0.1). The decision log, the global spec and STATUS are unchanged until you approve.

Your answers are in as settled (§9.1). Two things I added to the design that you haven't seen yet:

  • Judging repeated chunk lists once. The judge never sees the cutoff date, so a task with the same indicator and the same 5 chunks at several cutoffs is judged once and reused. That cuts 8,433 tasks to 7,685 judgments. It doesn't leak, because those chunks were eligible at every cutoff that retrieved them. Each call only holds tasks from one term and one cutoff, so no task ever sees another task's later chunks.
  • Two days of Gemini quota. At 10 tasks per call, the token-per-minute limit allows about 7 calls a minute, so the request limit is what binds. The first batch (all AIADMK cutoffs, DMK full term, TVK month 5) takes about one quota day. The second (DMK landmarks) takes the next. Quotas reset at 12:30 IST.

Five open points need your yes or no (§9.2):

  1. Who marks a promise as directional? I propose a one-time bulk pass over the promise text only. A promise containing any number can never count as directional. Both judges then use the same flag.
  2. "Diluted when even one indicator is diluted", taken literally? I'd apply it even when the promise's other indicators are not_started or fulfilled.
  3. Paying for Gemini if the DMK landmarks spill onto a third day (Oct 24). The global spec says no paid API. My default is to wait for the quota and ask you on the day.
  4. Minimum strong-judge coverage. I propose gold and headline promises are required. After those, I report the measured usage and you decide how far to go: the rest of TVK, then the flagged items.
  5. Letting the judging code read the gold sample. The strong-judge queue needs the gold promise IDs, which conflicts with spec 06's "nothing in the judging code reads data/gold/". I propose it may read only the ID columns of gold_sample.csv, never the labels, and spec 06 gets amended to match.

Gold labelling: the stage 05 spot-check sheet and report won't show verdicts for gold promises. Please also don't browse verdicts in the database until you've finished labelling, or your labels could be anchored by them.

Schedule: this is tight. Bulk judging runs Oct 22–23, the strong judge Oct 23–24 (only after both spot-checks are in), and stages 06–08 then fit into Oct 24–25. The cut order stays your call.

Once you answer the five points, I'll mark the spec approved, log the decisions, amend the global spec and CLAUDE.md, and update STATUS so Claude Code can start the build.

Claude's response

Your point 5 is a misunderstanding worth correcting before anything is built, so first the answer:

The gold set doesn't guide the judge. It grades it. It is test data (D-007, leakage rule 4). You label a random sample of promises by hand. Stage 06 then compares the bulk and strong judges' verdicts against your labels, which is how the whitepaper can say how accurate the LLM verdicts are (RQ5). If the judge saw the labels, as examples or as hints, the accuracy figure would be meaningless: it would be marking its own homework. The line in spec 06 enforces exactly that rule in code.

The one thing the judging code does need is the gold promise IDs (not your labels). Global §6.3 says Claude must also judge the gold promises, so both judges can be scored on the same items. That's why I proposed letting it read only the ID columns of gold_sample.csv. I've written it in that way.

# Judge whether a government commitment was put into effect, from the extracts only
