If an `indicator` is given, judge the indicator (it is one checkable part of the promise; the promise is there for context). Otherwise judge the promise itself.

# Mark directional commitments

Each item below is one commitment from an election manifesto, in English. Decide for each whether it is **directional**.

A commitment is **directional** if it commits only to effort or direction ("promote", "encourage", "strengthen", "take steps towards", "give importance to", "work for"), with no amount, target or list of parts.

It is **not directional** if it names something concrete that can be checked: an amount of money, a number of units or people, a target, a list of parts, or a named institution, scheme, building or law to be created or changed. Most commitments ("build a hospital in a named town", "give a monthly pa …

Judge only the text given. Do not use anything you know about any party, state or scheme.

cutoff that retrieved the list. A key's judging cutoff is the earliest configured cutoff of its term that
retrieved it, and calls group keys by (term, judging cutoff) only, so no task sees a chunk that was not
eligible at another task's cutoff.

- a selected verdict without a date, after a realised one, is replaced by the latest earlier realised verdict
  (status, date, citations), with `needs_review` and reason `non_monotone`.

"""Strong judge (spec 05 §4.9, D-086; global §6.2–§6.3): a priority queue judged by fresh Claude Code subagents.

Queue units are promise × cutoff with all their indicators, in priority order (deterministic within a level by
sha256(`promise_id@cutoff`)):
  P1 gold (IDs from gold_sample.csv only) and P2 headline, at full term (completed terms) or the current
  landmark (ongoing term); P3 the remaining promises of the ongoing term at its landmark; P4 bulk-flagged
  (`needs_review`) promises at full term; P5 flagged at the backtest term's landmarks; P6 flagged at the training
  term's landmarks. (Terms are picked by their §7 `role`, not by name.)

Batches (`judge.strong.tasks_per_batch`): one term and one cutoff per batch, a unit is never split, and a key is
judged once and reused only for units at the same or a later cutoff (so no judgment was made beside chunks dated
after a cutoff it is stored for). Files: data/judgments/{run_id}/in/batch_NNN.jsonl (tasks as rendered, aliases
only), …/out/batch_NNN.jsonl, …/manifest.json. A batch with failing tasks is re-run once with only those tasks

'''
s=s.replace(old,new)

Smoke test (--limit 20), four rounds. The first prompt failed both stop rules: 37% of first answers failed the checks, almost all on quotes. The model quoted document titles, shortened quotes with "...", and rewrote standard Government Order wording. Fixes: - Your decisions (logged as D-094): quote matching ignores "(Rupees … only)" glosses, and a failing task gets two tries alone; the 3% unresolved stop is unchanged. - My fixes (logged as D-095): - quotes may come from the document title, which the judge sees with each extract; - stricter quote instructions; - retries show the model which check failed. - Lenient relevance: reading verdicts against their chunks showed the judge credited an "urge the Union government" promise with an unrelated coaching-class order. The prompt now says a step only counts if it is about the same action and beneficiaries.

Final round: 10.6% first answers failed, 7 of 265 unresolved, leakage line 0, same prompt and model for every term. One known weakness remains: a budget speech saying money "has been provided" can still pass as fulfilled. The spot-check's group b is aimed at exactly that.

Other results: - Key count matches the spec: 8,433 tasks reduce to 7,685 distinct judgments. - Directional flags: the first version flagged about 40% of promises, including "urge" promises and concrete actions. The corrected one flags AIADMK 43/312, DMK 79/667, TVK 50/695. Some borderline flags remain; stage 06 will measure them against your gold tags. - Memory probe: none of the 40 tasks with no evidence got an answer claiming a status that needs evidence. - Retry fix mid-run: early in tier A, retries added 84% more calls because each mini-batch held under 2 tasks. I now pool failures per group, as spec 05 §4.5 describes. That started a new run, but earlier answers came from the cache. - Tests: 373 tests pass offline.

That works, and it fits the isolation rules: same prompt and checks, fresh subagents that see only their batch. It does change three things you should know about before I set it up.

  1. Mixed judges in the forward backtest. DMK landmark verdicts would come only from Claude. AIADMK (the training side of the forward backtest) and DMK's full term are judged by Gemini. So the forward backtest would train on one judge and test on another, and stage 06 can't measure that gap at landmarks (the gold labels are end-of-term). I'd record these rows as strong (Claude) and state it as a limitation in the whitepaper.
  2. Scale. Tier B is about 3,800 tasks, so about 190 batches of 20. Each subagent reads about 90k tokens, about 17M input tokens in total, roughly 20× the required P1 + P2 work. Run 5 at a time, that's about 3–4 hours.
  3. Timing. By D-080/D-086, Claude batches wait for both spot-checks. Your stage 04 verdicts arrive at 11:30. The stage 05 sheet can only be drawn once tier A is complete, around 14:00–15:00 IST. If that review leads to a prompt change, any tier B batches already run would be stale.

Your 21:00 reset adds one window, about 25 more batches.

Options for the rest of tier B (DMK landmarks), to decide before tomorrow:

  1. Gemini from 12:30 IST tomorrow for the batches Claude hasn't reached. First it finishes tier A's last TVK retries (about 30 calls), then about 470 calls cover roughly 2,500 tasks. Claude and Gemini together could finish tier B by tomorrow night. DMK landmarks would then have mixed judges, which I'd record per verdict (judge_source).
  2. Shrink tier B to months 12–48 (drop months 5 and 6, about a third of the tasks). Claude-only would still take about 2 more days.
  3. Keep going with Claude only and accept that tier B finishes about 25 Oct.

Nothing that matters is lost if the scratch folder goes.

What happens to it. The scratch folder sits under /private/tmp/…/scratchpad/, which belongs to this Claude Code session. macOS clears /private/tmp on reboot, and a new session, whether on another account or not, gets its own scratch folder and won't use this one. Until a reboot the files just stay on disk.

Which batch files it holds. sj/ has 271 staged batch folders, one per batch: 001–262 plus the retries 006_r, 033_r, 056_r, 093_r, 098_r, 104_r, 229_r, 239_r and 250_r. - Inputs: each folder has in/instructions.md, a copy of the prompt, and in/batch.md, the line-wrapped batch. - Outputs: most also have out/verdicts.jsonl, the subagent's answers.

What is lost. - Batch inputs: nothing. All 271 originals are in the repo under data/judgments/judge-20261022T070634Z/in/, and ept judge stage can rebuild any of them. - Subagent outputs: nothing. Every finished verdicts.jsonl was already copied to the repo's out/ and imported into the DB; none are left unimported. - Bookkeeping files: tokens.txt and sonnet.txt are already applied. Token counts sit in the manifest and the model is recorded on every DB row. - What actually goes: the helper scripts imp_all.sh, tok.py and gemini_day.sh (copies of the first two are committed in the repo), and the run logs: smoke tests, tier A and the Gemini day. Their key numbers are already in STATUS, spec 05 §10 and the run metadata. - Not yet in git: the latest manifest and the batch 254–260 outputs are on disk in the repo but uncommitted. They are safe, but should be committed.

How much of the global spec is left. - Stage 05 (judgment), roughly 90% done. Left: - P4 batches 261 and 262, then retries 255 and 257. - P5 if you want it: about 30 batches, optional. - Your verdicts on spotcheck_05.csv. - aggregate → final → report. - Docs and the closing commit. - Stage 04 (retrieval): only its closing notes in spec 04 §10. - Stage 06 (evaluation): not started in code. Spec 06 is still a draft and gold labelling is still in its own Cowork conversation. - Stage 07 (survival models: reverse and forward backtest, TVK projection): no spec, no code. - Stage 08 (website, whitepaper, deploy): no spec, no code.

How to give me the gold labels

The labels sit in the labels collection of the page's database in the other account. I can read an artifact database only if my account can open that artifact, and I need its link. Three ways, in my order of preference:

  1. Have the other account's Claude export the CSV into the project folder. Spec G6 already says that conversation writes data/gold/gold_labels.csv on request (complete rows only, tags folded into notes). Ask it to also write data/gold/gold_relabel.csv if the self-agreement check was done. If that session mounts the same project folder, there is nothing to transfer. I only read the CSV and don't touch the page. If it can't write to the folder, it can paste the CSV and you save it to that path.
  2. Share the artifact with this account. In the page's Share menu, add [REDACTED_EMAIL] with view access and send me the link. Cross-account or cross-organization sharing may be restricted, and then option 1 is the fallback.
  3. Add a download button to the page. That means republishing it with the downloads capability from the other account, which is more work than option 1.

Whichever you choose, only complete labels should come over. I will not label, suggest or check any gold item (G5.4). I only compute metrics from the labels.

What else stage 06 needs

A. Gold set tooling (Part 1) - Port draw_gold.py and gold_page_data.py to ept evaluate gold draw and gold-page-data. Criterion G9.1 requires the draw to reproduce byte for byte. - A label validator for G9.4, the overlap test against prompts/ for G5.2, and a check that ept.judge reads only the IDs in gold_sample.csv. - Approve the open items OQ-G1 to OQ-G4. OQ-G4 (labelling stops end of 2026-10-24) has already passed, so it needs a new date.

B. Metrics (Part 2, the part that isn't written) - Gold-versus-judge comparison, run separately for the bulk judge and the strong judge on the same gold promises. The comparison covers: - Full term for AIADMK and DMK, and TVK at month 5, with per-term and pooled results. - Weighted and unweighted figures, per G3. - Status accuracy and macro-F1 with a confusion matrix, and E1 (event or no event) precision, recall and F1. - Date error: median absolute days, and the share within ±30 and ±90 days. - Splits for directional versus other promises, vague versus specific, and in_corpus true versus false. - Wilson or bootstrap intervals, because the gold set will hold only about 40–78 promises. - Landmark validity. Gold dates imply "realised by month m" at each landmark, so I can score each judge's landmark verdicts against them. That is the input quality for the backtest. For AIADMK gold promises the strong judge ran only at full term, so landmarks measure bulk only. - Self-agreement. Status and E1 agreement between the first label and the re-label, plus the date difference (resolves Q-08). - Bulk-versus-strong agreement on every promise both judged (P2 to P4), as a wider check than gold alone.

C. Error analysis - Split each disagreement into retrieval miss, judge error, label ambiguity, or evidence outside the corpus. This needs the gold evidence chunk IDs checked against the top-5 retrieval. Stage 04 never measured retrieval recall against human evidence. - Compare the stage 05 directional flags with the gold [directional] tag. - Compare error rates across terms as a neutrality check. - Cite the memory probe (0/40 evidence-needing answers).

D. Outputs and hand-offs - Add ept evaluate and write reports/evaluation_06.md/json, plus a JSON export of the accuracy numbers for the website and whitepaper. - Give stage 07 measured error rates (E1 sensitivity and specificity, date error) so it can run a sensitivity analysis on the backtest. - Finish spec 06, then log the decisions.

E. Constraints and corrections - Gold labels can't tune anything (leakage rule 4). Part 2 can only report errors, never trigger a prompt change or re-judging. The spec must say so. - Decision numbering: the draft proposes D-081 to D-086, which clash with the log. I used D-098 and D-099 today, so the gold decisions need to become D-100 and up. The gold conversation was told to start at D-098, so pass that on. - Judge models: the gold promises (P1) were judged by Claude Opus. TVK and the other strong levels ran partly on Sonnet. I can't measure the Opus-versus-Sonnet gap from the gold set. I'll state that as a limitation. - Process: CLAUDE.md says one stage per conversation. You asked for this in the current one, so I'll go ahead, but the code could move to a new conversation if you prefer.

I've written the full spec 06 (Part 2 is new, in specs/06-evaluation.md, not committed yet). It also needs your approval.

Schedule

Doing evaluation and deployment first is possible, but it would leave the site with only the verdict ledger. I suggest this order instead, with nothing cut: 1. Now to 22:00: spec 07 and its code (survival curves, Cox model, reverse backtest, TVK projection). It uses the final verdicts and doesn't depend on the gold labels. 2. In parallel: stage 06 code (ept evaluate), tested on fixtures while your labels come in. 3. 22:00: I run stage 06 on your labels and write the report. 4. Overnight to Monday: spec 08, then the site, then deploy. The accuracy page fills from reports/evaluation_06.json. 5. Monday evening to Tuesday morning: whitepaper text and the end-to-end check.

If time runs short, the cut order applies from item 3 downward (forward backtest, then TVK projection). Never cut the evaluation or the reverse backtest.

Metrics, kept viva-friendly

  • Primary: E1 agreement. A 2×2 table of judge against human (realised, or not). It gives accuracy, recall, precision and specificity, each with a 95% Wilson interval. The report prints the raw counts so you can recompute any figure.
  • Secondary: exact 7-status match, with a confusion matrix. A second line treats not_started and unverifiable as the same.
  • Date error: the median days off, the signed median (judge late or early), and the share within 90 days.
  • Also reported:
  • Agreement at each landmark month.
  • Splits by directional, vague and in_corpus.
  • Bulk judge against strong judge.
  • Your label against your re-label (the ceiling for any judge).
  • The directional flag against your tag.
  • Deliberately left out: significance tests, macro-F1, kappa and bootstrap. With about 20 labels per term the intervals are wide, and the report says so.
  • Error buckets, assigned automatically: evidence outside the corpus, uncertain label, retrieval miss, judge error. Gold labels never change a verdict or prompt.

A Cox model with five covariates: promise type, cost band, vague vs specific, depends on the Union government, continues an existing scheme. sector stays descriptive because it has 13 levels with several tiny groups. A bootstrap band for the projection.
  • Event and time: E1 (realised, with a date) is primary and E2 (fulfilled only) is a sensitivity run. Time is counted in days from the swearing-in. Year-only or month-only dates use the middle of the period.
  • Reverse backtest (never cut): I fit on DMK-2021 only. AIADMK's state at each landmark month comes from its landmark verdicts. For each promise not yet realised I predict the chance it is realised by later months. I compare the predicted share with what AIADMK actually delivered, against a no-covariate baseline. The scores are the average gap in percentage points and a concordance number.
  • TVK projection: the observed month-5 share plus the expected additional share, with an 80% band from refitting on resampled DMK promises. The band shows fitting uncertainty only.
  • Forward backtest: the same code with the terms swapped, built only if time allows.

The main risk

The terms look very different at month 5, and part of that may be the judge rather than the governments:

Term Judge Realised by month 5
DMK-2021 Claude 4.8%
TVK-2026 Claude 3.3%
AIADMK-2016 Gemini 34.6%

At full term AIADMK is 86.5% realised against DMK's 61.2%. A model trained on DMK will likely under-predict AIADMK's early delivery, so the backtest measures model error plus judge difference. I've written this into the spec as a limitation. Stage 06 will measure how far Gemini and Claude differ on your gold promises, which bounds it. The only alternative is judging more AIADMK promises with Claude. That is the P5 work you dropped.

Questions for you (all in §9)

  1. Headline TVK model: DMK-trained as primary, with the pooled and AIADMK-only models shown as the range. Or pooled as primary?
  2. Judge gap: state it as a limitation and quantify it in stage 06 (my proposal), or spend Claude budget on more AIADMK strong batches?
  3. Covariates: are the five above acceptable?
  4. lifelines: may I pip install it?
  5. Forward backtest: build it after the reverse one if time allows?

Once you approve, I'll log D-110 to D-113 and build.

Turn 165

It feels like choosing only DMK model was biased due to the realisation rate similarity. How do I stop such bias from creeping in? I can't run Claude batches a lot - if a Haiku run suffices then we might be able to do it, but still the 3000ish promises will drain my token limit. Covariates seem ok, lifelines sure, but forward backtest is certainly on the cut for now. For the bias part, is still DMK model the best way to go ahead? Also, does the model update on how well the govt. has fared in the earlier months while predicting recent months? I hope so

Claude's response

Short answers first, then I'll update the spec.

1. Is choosing DMK biased? Yes. I proposed DMK partly because its month-5 rate resembles TVK's. That is picking the model that matches the target's early outcome, which is the kind of bias to avoid. A better rule is one fixed before looking at TVK, which treats both completed terms the same way.

2. A correction to my own claim. I attributed the AIADMK/DMK gap to the judge, but only the early months are affected. Landmark realised shares, from the final data:

Month DMK AIADMK Who judged DMK
5 4.8% 34.6% Claude
12 15.9% 41.0% Mostly Claude
24 39.4% 59.6% Mostly Gemini, like AIADMK
36 49.9% 72.8% Mostly Gemini, like AIADMK
48 57.9% 82.4% Mostly Gemini, like AIADMK

From month 24 both terms are judged by Gemini, and AIADMK is still 20–25 points higher. That gap looks real, for example 83 AIADMK promises continue existing schemes. Only months 5–12 are judge-contaminated.

3. Stopping bias in the design. - The model rule is fixed in the spec before any backtest runs. - The headline uses both terms with equal weight and separate baselines per term. DMK-only and AIADMK-only are shown as the range, and no one is picked by resemblance. - Conditioning on "not realised by month 5" removes most of the early-month level difference, because only the shape after month 5 matters.

4. Does the model update on how the government fared so far? In v0.1 only partly. Promises already realised stay realised, but the pace of the future months came from history unchanged. I'll add an explicit pace update. Pace factor = (observed events by month 5 + 20) / (events the model expected by month 5 + 20). The 20 is a prior that shrinks a noisy factor toward 1. The factor multiplies future hazards. The reverse backtest can test it honestly. At each AIADMK landmark I compare the error with and without the update, and the constant 20 is fixed in advance.

5. Haiku or more Claude batches? I don't recommend it. Judging the 312 AIADMK promises at all 7 cutoffs would be ~120 batches (~20M tokens). Even full term plus month 5 only is ~35 batches. A third judge would also add a new inconsistency, and Haiku's performance on the strict quote and date checks is untested. The pace update and stage 06's measured gap on your gold promises cover the problem more cheaply.

Backtest results (DMK model → AIADMK)

  • Pace update helps. The average error drops from 14.5 to 6.7 points when predicting from month 5 (12.1 to 10.2 from month 12). The no-covariate baseline scores 16.8 and 12.9.
  • The model under-predicts AIADMK throughout. From month 5 it predicts 78.5% realised by month 48, against 85.3% observed.
  • Covariates add little. Concordance is 0.563, where 0.5 is chance. Without the pace update the covariate model is barely better than the baseline.
  • Date rule matters at month 5. The month-5 error is 1.2 points with period-end dates and 6.8 with period-start dates. The report prints both.

The problem with the TVK projection

The pace factor for TVK came out at 0.17, which pushes the projection to 19% realised by month 60, against 65% with no update. The cause is a mismatch. The model's expected count at month 5 comes from hindsight event dates, while TVK's 3.3% is only what is documented so far:

Term Hindsight share by month 5 Documented at month 5
DMK 19.6% 4.8%
AIADMK 51.0% 34.6%

So part of the "slow start" is documentation lag, not slow delivery. I haven't changed the rule you approved, because changing it after seeing TVK's output would be the bias you want to avoid.

Decision for you

  • A. Keep the rule and show both lines. The website shows 19% (with update) and 65% (without), flagged as bounds. It is honest but a very wide range for your headline result.
  • B. Calibrate the pace factor only against a term judged by the same judge at month 5. That is DMK, since both it and TVK were judged by Claude at month 5, while AIADMK was judged by Gemini. For DMK, 4.8% is the documented share at month 5, so TVK's 3.3% gives k near 0.8. The rule comes from the judge-source table, not from TVK's outcome. I would log it as a post-hoc, outcome-informed change, and the report would say so.

I recommend B, logged transparently, with A's numbers kept in the report as the original pre-specified result. Which do you want?

Assumptions stated before each line

The report (SCENARIO_TEXT in report.py) and the site will carry these: - No update: TVK follows the historical average pace regardless of its first five months. - A: the historical average predicts how many promises should be realised by month 5, and TVK's relative speed continues. Weakness: the expectation uses hindsight dates, while TVK's 3.3% counts only what is documented. Part of the slowness is documentation lag. - B: TVK's documented month-5 count is compared with DMK's documented month-5 share (4.8%). Both were judged by Claude at that landmark; AIADMK was judged by Gemini. Weakness: I wrote this rule after seeing A's result, so it is labelled post-hoc (D-114). It also rests on one term, and its k is applied to hindsight-based hazards.

The local site is built and committed (4847bad, 394 tests pass). Preview it at http://localhost:8765 (I left a static server running on your Mac), or run python3 -m http.server -d site/public.

What's on the site

  • Overview:
  • Headline cards for each term.
  • Kaplan-Meier curves, with dots for what was documented at each landmark month.
  • The TVK projection with all three lines, bands, and a "Assumes / Weakness" box under each.
  • A note that the terms were judged by different mixes of judges.
  • A backtest accuracy card.
  • Promise explorer: all 1,674 promises, searchable and filterable by term, sector, type, status, month and judge. Each opens to the rationale, the verbatim evidence quotes with links to the official sources, and the status at each landmark.
  • Whitepaper: 11 sections, with every number read from the data files. The accuracy table fills in automatically once the evaluation exists. Until then it shows a "will appear" note.
  • Data: promises.json is 2.6 MB, and the whole site is 2.8 MB. No gold labels are exported.
  • Mobile: the checks I could run suggest it works, but the headless screenshot was cropped by Chrome's minimum window width, so I haven't confirmed phone layout.

Still open

  1. Gold labels. I'm still waiting for the CSV. Open the original page, tap Export CSV, and paste the result here. Stage 06 and the site's accuracy numbers depend on it.
  2. Publish check and repo. I haven't created anything on GitHub.   3. Docs. I still need to update STATUS and the decision log for spec 07 and spec 08 (D-115 to D-117). I'll do that with the final commit.

Yes, it gives a better comparison between the terms, and it's cheap, so I've already started it. It's running now in the background.

What's running

  • Only DMK months 5 and 6 are missing on the Gemini model. Its verdicts for months 12 to full term, all of AIADMK and TVK month 5 already exist.
  • The run covers 1,315 judging keys, about 130 calls and an estimated 15 minutes.
  • It uses zero Claude tokens. If the Gemini daily quota stops it, it resumes after the 12:30 IST reset.
  • It writes only to the bulk run. Today's final verdicts, the model report and the site don't change, because final prefers Claude's verdicts.

Why it helps

Right now DMK's early months are Claude-judged while AIADMK's are Gemini-judged. That is the 4.8% against 34.6% problem at month 5, and it makes the backtest compare unlike things. With Gemini on all three terms, DMK against AIADMK is like for like. TVK month 5 is also already Gemini-judged, so the pace comparison becomes like for like too. Scenario B's "matched judge" idea then holds for every term.

What it doesn't do

It makes the terms comparable, not more accurate. On your 40 labels Gemini over-claims. Specificity was 50% (5 of 10 not-realised promises called realised), against Claude's 100%. Its TVK month-5 share is 23% against Claude's 3.3%, so the TVK headline would change a lot depending on which judge you believe. Neither judge has a TVK accuracy measurement.

What I'll do next

  1. When the run finishes, aggregate the new verdicts and build a second set of final verdicts using Gemini only for every term. It will have its own file, separate from the Claude-preferred one.
  2. Run the survival models, backtest and projection on both. The overview page and the whitepaper will show the two judge settings side by side (Claude-preferred and Gemini-consistent), each with its assumptions. I won't pick one as the truth.
  3. Re-check the stage 06 numbers for the Gemini-only set against your 40 labels.

If you'd rather show only one setting, tell me. I'd still keep both in the whitepaper, because the gap between them is itself a finding about how much the answer depends on the judge.

Yes, the Claude-only run is feasible, and the batches are already exported (committed as 21fa292).

The 11-hour Claude run

  • Cost per batch: Sonnet 5.5 batches have averaged 166k subagent tokens each (62 measured). Earlier windows gave about 20–25 batches each, so three windows is roughly 60–75 batches.
  • Needed and exported (64 new batches):
  • Full-term verdicts, AIADMK (12 batches): batches 263–274.
  • Full-term verdicts, DMK (18 batches): batches 275–292.
  • AIADMK month 5 (20 batches): batches 293–312.
  • AIADMK month 6 (14 batches): batches 313–326.
  • DMK month 12 is already exported in batches 108–110 (3 batches).
  • Run order: full terms, then AIADMK month 5, then batches 108–110, then AIADMK month 6. The first three groups come to 53 batches, and month 6 adds 14 for 67 in total. That fits your windows, but only if the limit allows about 22 batches per window.
  • What is not feasible: AIADMK months 12–48 (about 96 batches) and DMK months 24–48 (about 105). So the Claude-only setting is not a complete judging of everything.
  • What Claude-only supports: the survival curves, the Cox model and the TVK projection (they use full-term plus month-5 states). The reverse backtest would have only two landmarks, months 5 and 6.
  • Needs from you: this session must stay open on the Mac. I'd run batches one at a time and, when a limit hits, wait and retry until the windows are used. I need a command to start at 22:00. I'll also prepare the --strong-only final variant and the model and site changes tonight, so the results are ready within an hour of the last batch.
  • Fallback: I recommend publishing the current site tomorrow after your review, then updating it after the run, so a failed run doesn't leave you with nothing live.

Rating the project, unbiased

Strong: - The scope is unusually large for a course project: 9,254 documents, 1,674 promises, three terms, a judge pipeline, a hand-labelled evaluation, a backtest and a projection. - The discipline is rare: leakage rules enforced in code, a spec-first process, 120 logged decisions, 394 tests, and limitations stated openly. - It is reproducible and published.

Weak: - The headline comparison (87% vs 61% realised) isn't interpretable, because the judge changes the answer. TVK at month 5 is 3.3% or 22.9% depending on the judge. - The accuracy evidence is thin: n=40, no TVK promises, and dates are off by 5–6 months. - Promise covariates explain little. - The TVK projection spans 19–71%, which is honest but not a result. Scenario B and the pace update were chosen after seeing outputs, which I flagged. - Much of the engineering sits outside what a course expects and is hard to see in the output.

My overall view: about 8/10 for effort and rigor, and 5–6/10 for substantive conclusions. It stands out as a course project through its measurement honesty and engineering, but not through its findings. The findings are that judge choice dominates and that timing is hard to measure, which is a legitimate result.

Purpose: be able to explain, defend and criticise every method in the project **in your own words**. ---

## 0. The 90-second story
1. **Question.** Do Tamil Nadu governments realise their manifesto promises, how fast, and what does the past imply for TVK (2026–)?
2. **Data.** 1,674 promises from three manifestos; 9,254 official English documents (60,259 passages) from tn.gov.in and archived copies.
3. **Measurement.** For each promise, find the 5 most relevant passages available by a given date, and have a language model decide a status and a date, forced to quote the passages. 
4. **Validation.** Worst-case spot-checks at every stage, plus a random stratified hand-labelled set (n = 40) as the only unbiased accuracy estimate.
5. **Analysis.** Time-to-event analysis: Kaplan–Meier curves, a Cox model, a backtest (fit on DMK, predict AIADMK) and a TVK projection.

The viva sheet and the "Work done" page are both done. Tests pass again (394, exit code checked) and everything is committed.

Viva sheet: docs/VIVA_SHEET.md

It is gitignored, so it stays private and never goes in the public repo.

  • Survival analysis:
  • Event, right-censoring and the non-informative-censoring assumption.
  • Survival, hazard and cumulative hazard, and the link S = exp(−H).
  • Kaplan–Meier with the Greenwood variance and a worked example.
  • The Cox model: the partial likelihood, Efron ties, what a hazard ratio is and isn't, and stratified Cox.
  • Schoenfeld residuals and the concordance index.
  • The backtest and conditional survival.
  • The pace factor, derived as a Gamma–Poisson posterior mean.
  • The percentile bootstrap, and why not Weibull or competing risks.
  • Evaluation: the confusion matrix with our counts, the four rates and why not kappa, the Wilson interval with its formula and a worked example, and the stratified sample with post-stratification weights. It also covers the n=40 limit, date accuracy, and why the final verdicts score higher than either judge alone.
  • Retrieval and language models: chunking and the availability date, the BM25 formula, dense retrieval, reciprocal rank fusion, the judge's guardrails and what they don't prove, the memory probe, and hindsight versus documented dates.
  • 30 hard questions with answers, a verified numbers card, and seven things to do before the viva, such as redoing the Kaplan–Meier example by hand.

Two things to know before you rely on it: 1. Weak points it tells you to state yourself. A few proportional-hazards tests do reject (AIADMK advocacy p=0.008, law/regulation 0.024, and continues-existing in the two-term model 0.028). Scenario B was added after seeing A's result. The date gap of 5–6 months has no isolated cause, and the sheet lists the likely ones as unverified hypotheses. 2. Verify, don't memorise. I wrote the sheet from the code and reports, but you should check each formula yourself against reports/modelling_07.md and the code. That is the point of the practice list at the end.

"Work done" page: work.html

It is linked from the nav and from the top of the whitepaper, and all counts come from data/work.json, computed at export time: - Numbers: 9,254 documents, 60,259 passages, 1,674 promises, 8,433 evidence searches, 155 Claude batches run (326 prepared), 23M subagent tokens, 120 decisions, 394 tests, 15,879 lines of Python. - Content: eight stage cards with what was built and how it was checked, a timeline, a "how the work was organised" section, and links to the specs, decision log and reports. - Who did what: it also states plainly what was Claude's work and what was yours. - Layout: I checked it only in a headless desktop screenshot, not on a phone.

Turn 182

Why don't we modify the promise explorer part to let the public post their judgements on the promises' level of completion? We can show that the website is geared to store these separately as well? I just picked this idea from the DMK tracker on pudhiyavan.com. Will this work? Will it complicate stuff? Is it possible to do?

Claude's response

Yes, it's possible, but a live "post your judgement" box is not a small addition. It would change what kind of project this is.

Why it isn't trivial

The site is static, hosted on GitHub Pages, with no server and no database. Accepting public input needs somewhere to store it.

  • A live voting or comment box needs a third-party backend (Supabase, Firebase or similar) and a public key in the page's code. It also needs anti-spam and abuse rules, moderation, and a privacy statement, because you would be collecting user data. Estimate: three to five hours plus testing, with a real risk of breaking things the night before a Tuesday 13:00 deadline.
  • Neutrality risk: a political tracker with open voting invites brigading, with each side pushing its own promises' scores. That would sit uneasily next to the "no rankings, evidence beside every status" rule the whole site follows. It would also need protecting from fake or duplicate votes.
  • Statistical validity: self-selected votes are not a representative sample. You can show them as "what visitors said", but you can't present them as a measurement.
  • Leakage rules: crowd judgements must never feed the judges, prompts or models, the same as your gold labels. Keeping them separate is easy, and it is a good thing to state.
  • Viva angle: an examiner could ask how you handle bias, spam and label quality in crowd data. A feature you haven't tested for those is a liability.

A cheap version that gets most of the value

  1. "Suggest a correction" on each promise opens a pre-filled GitHub Issue (or a Google Form) containing the promise ID, its current status and an evidence link field.
  2. You moderate. Nothing appears on the site automatically.
  3. Stored separately: submissions live in the repo's issues (or the form's sheet), never mixed into verdicts. A small script can export approved ones to community.json, which the explorer shows as "N community suggestions", clearly labelled and unverified.
  4. Cost: roughly an hour, with no backend, no keys and no privacy problem beyond GitHub's own. Contributors need a GitHub account if you use Issues, and the Google Form avoids that but adds a Google dependency.

What I'd put in the whitepaper

A short "Future work: community input" design describing the live version: the data schema, strict separation from judge verdicts, a rule that community labels are never used in judging or fitting, anti-abuse measures, and moderation. It shows the site is built to be extended that way, with no code or risk now.

My recommendation

Do the pre-filled "Suggest a correction" link plus the future-work design, and skip the live voting backend for this submission. Say which you want (GitHub Issues or Google Form), or "future-work text only", and I'll add it before publishing. I haven't looked at how pudhiyavan.com implements theirs, so I can't say how closely this matches it.

Claude's response

Do both in the UI conversation, with two rules attached.

Main-page charts and layout (UI conversation). This is presentation work. Charts must read their numbers from the exported JSON. If you want an aggregate that isn't exported yet, for example a status split by term and month, the UI conversation should list it and I'll add it to the exporter here. The summary data already has status counts per term and month, so most charts need no change.

One design note, which you may overrule. A pie chart is fine for one term's status split at one date, but pies are poor for comparing terms or months. For "how do the three terms compare", a 100% stacked horizontal bar per term works better: the same seven statuses, one bar per term, read side by side. Seven slices is also at the edge of what a pie handles. Mention that to the UI conversation and let it propose both.

Rewording the whitepaper (UI conversation, with a guard). Wording and structure are fine to change there. Add this to the prompt you paste:

You may reword and restructure the whitepaper text for clarity. Do not change any factual claim, number, method description, limitation or caveat, and do not delete or soften a limitation. If a sentence's meaning changes, say so. List every sentence whose meaning could have changed, so the main conversation can check it against the specs. Any figure must remain data-bound from the JSON.

The reason is that the whitepaper is what you will be questioned on. A reworded sentence that quietly turns "most likely" into "because", or drops the post-hoc label on scenario B, creates a viva problem. After the rewrite, read the changed paragraphs against docs/VIVA_SHEET.md.

Judging bias can't be removed, only bracketed. A single judge removes the mismatch between terms, but not that judge's own bias. On your 40 labels Gemini over-claims, with recall 67% and specificity 50%. Claude under-claims, with precision 100% and recall 40%. So "Gemini-only" is consistent across terms but still tilted upward.

What the overview can honestly present

Present results as what holds under every judge versus what moves with the judge.

Holds under both existing settings (Gemini-only and Claude-preferred): - Direction of the covariate effects, from the pooled Cox model:

Characteristic Claude-preferred Gemini-only
Vague promises (hazard ratio) 1.95 2.34
Union-dependent promises 0.43 0.38
Advocacy promises 2.75 3.01

Vague and advocacy promises are realised faster, and Union-dependent ones slower, in both. - AIADMK ahead of DMK at the end of the term (87% vs 61% or 65%). - Weak ranking power: the concordance is about 0.56 in both. - Timing blur: the date gap is the same under every judge.

Moves with the judge: - The level of "realised". TVK at month 5 is 3.3% or 22.9%, and the month-60 projection ranges from 19% to 71%. - Whether the backtest's pace update helps.

What the Claude subagent runs add

They give a second pure single-judge setting, a strict one, to sit beside the lenient Gemini-only one. For the quantities that need only full-term and month-5 states, it would support: - End-of-term shares for both completed terms. - Kaplan–Meier, the Cox model and the TVK projection, with TVK month 5 already Claude-judged. - A reverse backtest at months 5 and 6 only, with one strict judge for both terms. That tests whether the pace update still helps when the judge doesn't change.

With a lenient bound (Gemini-only) and a strict bound (Claude-only), the overview can show TVK as a range ("between X% and Y% by month 60, depending on the judge"). It can also state which findings are identical across the two. That is more defensible in a viva than choosing one number.

What I'd change on the overview

  • Lead with a "robust findings" panel: the points above, each with both settings' numbers side by side.
  • Replace the three-way toggle with a two-way comparison (Gemini-only vs Claude-only). The current "Claude-preferred" setting mixes judges per term, so it is the least principled view. I'd keep it in the explorer and whitepaper only, as the best-evidence combination.
  • Judge-dependent numbers sit in a clearly separate block, shown as ranges.

Caveat

Until the run completes, I don't know what the Claude-only numbers will say. If the two settings disagree on a direction we currently think is robust, the robust-findings panel shrinks. That would be a finding too, but it needs checking after the run.

If you want, I'll add the "robust findings" table to the exporter now, so the UI conversation can design around it and the data fills automatically once the Claude-only results exist.

Two parts shouldn't be toggles, because a toggle hides the comparison. A visitor sees one setting at a time, and the point of the project is that the two settings can be compared.

Suggested structure

  1. Robust findings first. A short panel that states what holds under both judges (direction of effects, AIADMK ahead at term end, weak predictability) and what moves with the judge. It carries the main message, so it comes before any chart.
  2. Toggle (Claude-only / Gemini-only) for the single-setting views: end-of-term shares and the Kaplan–Meier curves. Those read naturally one setting at a time.
  3. Side by side, no toggle, for the two comparisons.
  4. Cox hazard ratios: one forest plot with two markers per characteristic, one for each judge. Agreement is visible at a glance, and a toggle would hide it.
  5. TVK projection: both settings' bands on one chart, so "depends on the judge" appears as a spread. The assumption boxes stay, with scenario B labelled post-hoc.
  6. Accuracy: how well each judge matched your 40 labels (precision, recall, date gap) and the limits of that test. This is what explains why the settings differ.

I think the pace update is worth keeping, but only as an indicator, not as a projection. Your goal ("is TVK on pace with previous governments?") is a fair question, and a more defensible way exists to show it.

What the evidence says about the pace update

  • As a predictor, it is not validated. In the backtest it cut the month-5 error from 14.5 to 6.7 points only when DMK and AIADMK were judged by different judges. With one judge for both, it made things slightly worse (14.7 to 16.0). So it can't be sold as a better forecast.
  • As a like-for-like pace comparison, it is sound. Compare TVK's documented count after five months with what earlier governments had documented at the same point, judged by the same judge. That is scenario B, now the sensible one. Scenario A mixes hindsight with documented, which is why it gives a nonsensical 0.17.

What it says under each judge (scenario B)

Setting TVK pace factor 80% interval Reading
Claude-preferred 0.81 0.66–0.97 slightly below earlier pace
Gemini-only 0.91 0.83–1.00 roughly in line, slightly below

The intervals come from the same Gamma–Poisson model as the pace factor, so they reflect how few events TVK has (23 under Claude, 159 under Gemini). Both settings point the same way: TVK is tracking at roughly 80–90% of the earlier governments' documented pace after five months, with the Claude-judged figure much less certain. That is the sentence for your MVP, and it is less judge-sensitive than the projected percentages.

Suggested simplification

  1. A "pace so far" strip, above the projection. For each setting, one marker for TVK's pace factor with its interval, against 1.0 for "same as earlier governments". Under it, the documented share at month 5 for AIADMK, DMK and TVK, all by the same judge. No model is needed to read it.
  2. The projection chart shows two lines per setting, not four in one plot:
  3. Historical pace (the old "no update").
  4. Current pace persists, which is scenario B.

I'd draw these as two small side-by-side panels, one per judge, rather than one crowded plot. 3. Scenario A leaves the overview. It stays in the whitepaper with the explanation of why its expectation is hindsight-based, so the pre-specified result is still disclosed and nothing looks cherry-picked. 4. Label the extrapolation honestly. "If TVK's current pace persists" is an extrapolation from five months and is untested as a forecast. The backtest evidence goes beside it.

For the viva, say the pace factor is a ratio of observed to expected events with a shrinkage prior. Its main use is the interval around "behind, in line, or ahead", not the extended curve.

If you agree, I'll add the pace-strip data (factor, interval, same-judge month-5 shares per term) to the exporter and tell the UI conversation which two lines per setting to draw. For Claude-only, B will use the Claude-judged AIADMK month-5 verdicts once those batches exist.

What I changed

  • Pace indicator data
  • data/pace.json now holds TVK's documented month-5 count, the documented month-5 shares of each term under the same judge, and the pace factor with its 80% interval.
  • Claude-preferred: k = 0.81 (0.65–0.97). Gemini-only: k = 0.92 (0.83–1.00).

  • Data contract for the new overview: summary_gemini.json, summary_claude.json, model_gemini.json, model_claude.json and pace.json. Each starts with meta: {setting, standin}. The Claude files are a stand-in (copies of the Claude-preferred data, standin: true) until the Claude-only run exists.

  • Docs: the new order, the pace-strip rules and the "scenario A leaves the overview" decision are in the specs and the decision log. I didn't edit the whitepaper text itself, since that goes to the UI conversation under the guard rule.

FOLLOW-UP: overview redesign decisions (2026-10-26). This extends your current design direction: keep every
design decision already made in this conversation (palette, typography, tone, components) unless a point
below forces a change. Work on branch `ui`; do not publish, push or touch the pipeline. Pull the latest main
into `ui` first (git merge main): it contains new data files and specs.

READ FIRST: specs/08-website.md section 11 and specs/07-survival-modelling.md section 12 (and D-121 in
docs/decisions/log.md).

DATA CONTRACT (site/public/data/, generated by `python -m ept export-site`; never hand-edit)
- summary_gemini.json, summary_claude.json, model_gemini.json, model_claude.json, pace.json,
  plus promises.json, evaluation.json, work.json. Every per-setting file begins with
  meta: {setting, standin}. *_claude.json is a STAND-IN (meta.standin = true) until the Claude-only run
  finishes: when standin is true, show a small "preliminary" tag on anything drawn from it.
- model_*.json: km, cox, backtest, projection (incl. projection.pace), limitations. backtest.landmarks entries
  can have unavailable:true (the Claude-only setting will cover months 5 and 6 only): handle that gracefully
  ("not available in this setting").
- pace.json: {gemini, claude, claude_preferred_mixed}: observed, n, observed_share, matched_terms,
  documented_share_by_term, expected, k, k_lo, k_hi (80% interval), p_k_ge_1.
- Old files (summary.json, model.json, *_bulk.json) still exist for the explorer/whitepaper.

NEW OVERVIEW STRUCTURE (in this order)
1. ROBUST FINDINGS panel first. Two short columns: "Holds under both judges" (vague and advocacy promises realised
   faster, Union-dependent slower, AIADMK ahead of DMK at end of term, promise characteristics rank poorly
   (concordance about 0.56), dates approximate by 5-6 months) and "Depends on the judge" (the level of
   'realised', TVK's level, the projection range, whether the pace update helps). Derive every number from the
   JSON files; no hand-typed figures.
2. TOGGLE Claude-only / Gemini-only (one toggle, one state for the whole section) for: end-of-term shares
   (term cards) and the Kaplan-Meier curves.
3. SIDE BY SIDE, no toggle: (a) Cox hazard ratios as ONE forest plot, two markers per characteristic
   (Gemini-only, Claude-only), reference line at 1; (b) the TVK projection as TWO small panels, one per setting.
4. PACE STRIP above the projection: for each setting one marker for k with its 80% interval against 1.0 ("same pace
   as earlier governments"), and the documented month-5 shares of AIADMK, DMK and TVK under that same judge.
   One-sentence reading under it: TVK is tracking at roughly 80-90% of earlier governments' documented pace after
   5 months (state the numbers from pace.json; the Claude-judged interval is wider because there are only 23 events).
5. PROJECTION PANELS: per setting two lines only: "historical pace" (projection.no_update) and
   "if TVK's current pace persists" (projection.matched_update), with the bootstrap bands. Label the second
   clearly: "an extrapolation from five months, not validated as a forecast". Do NOT show scenario A
   (projection.pace_update) on the overview; it stays in the whitepaper. The backtest evidence (pace update
   helped only when the two terms had different judges) goes in a short note beside it.
6. ACCURACY: how each judge matched the 40 hand labels (precision, recall, date gap), with the limits (n = 40,
   no TVK labels). Aggregate numbers only (evaluation.json); never any per-promise gold data.
7. WORK DONE: a link or short strip to work.html only. Do not put that content back on the overview.

The Claude-only setting is finished and committed (b6a5c87, 400 tests pass), with 8 promises excluded because their tasks never passed the checks.

The final batches

  • All 5 tasks failed again. The judge's checks rejected them on dates and quotes (J3, J5, J6), after two or three attempts each. That cost about 111k tokens. I did not retry further.
  • 8 promises are excluded from the Claude-only analysis: AIADMK 0151, 0154, 0299, and DMK 0257, 0284, 0312, 0536, 0664. The coverage is 309 of 312 for AIADMK, 662 of 667 for DMK and 695 of 695 for TVK. The list is stored in the output, and the analysis refuses a gap above 1%.
  • Two bugs fixed on the way:
  • "Done" tasks in the export now means a verdict exists, not that the task was in an imported batch.
  • The pace matching counted AIADMK month 5 (33 of 312 promises under Claude) as a matched term. It now needs at least 90% coverage.

Claude-only results

Claude-only Gemini-only Claude-preferred
Realised by end of term: AIADMK / DMK 52% / 30% 87% / 65% 87% / 61%
TVK at month 5 3.3% 22.9% 3.3%
Hazard ratio: vague / Union-dependent / advocacy 1.49 / 0.28 / 3.66 2.34 / 0.38 / 3.01 1.95 / 0.43 / 2.75
Concordance 0.52 0.57 0.56
Pace factor (80%) 0.81 (0.65–0.97) 0.92 (0.83–1.00) 0.81 (0.65–0.97)
TVK at month 60, no update / current pace 37% / 31% 71% / 69% 65% / 58%
  • What holds under all three judges: the direction of every covariate effect, with AIADMK ahead of DMK at the end of term and TVK just under the earlier pace. Concordance is near chance everywhere.
  • What moves: the level of "realised" is far lower under Claude alone. AIADMK is 52% against 87%, and the TVK projection ranges from 31% to 71%.
  • Backtest: unavailable for Claude-only, because Claude judged only a small share of AIADMK at months 5 and 6.

Data and docs

  • Site data: summary_claude.json and model_claude.json are now real (standin is false). Summary cells carry n, of and complete, so AIADMK month 5 (33 of 312) is marked incomplete.
  • Docs: D-123 is logged. STATUS and spec 07 have the update.
  • Viva sheet: its numbers predate the Claude-only setting, so refresh the numbers card.

  • Work done and data:

The cut at month 48 was a bug in how I exported the Kaplan–Meier curve. It affected AIADMK in both settings, not only Claude-only. It's fixed and committed (a778c84, 400 tests pass).

Cause: I exported curve points only at fixed months (5, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48 and 60). AIADMK's term lasted 59.4 months, so the month-60 point was dropped and the line stopped at 48. The last 11 months were never drawn. DMK's term was 60.06 months, so it kept its point.

Fix: - Export: the curve now has a point for every month plus one at the exact end of each term. AIADMK ends at month 59.43 and DMK at 60.06. - Endpoints: Claude-only AIADMK now ends at 52%, matching the 160 of 309 promises realised. Gemini-only ends at 87%. - Page text: the chart summary now reads "reaches 87% by the end of its term (month 59)".

What this does not change: the table values at months 5 to 48, the hazard ratios, the backtest and the projection. Those never used the plotted curve.

Not checked: I verified the data and the page text. I didn't look at the chart itself by eye, so check that the lines now run to the right-hand end.

Fixed and committed (f42921e, 400 tests pass, exit code checked).

Cause: your browser held an older promises.json from before I added the two-judge blocks. The old file has no Gemini history (g), and the page reads p.g[...] as soon as it loads. For a completed term that reads the key "0", so you saw "reading '0'". The current data file is correct, and I reproduced the page loading fine from it.

What to do now: hard-reload the explorer once (Cmd+Shift+R). If the old file is still being served, restart your static server from site/public.

What I changed so this can't recur: - Every data file is now fetched with revalidation, so a cached older file is never mixed with the newer pages. - If the explorer ever does get an old-shaped file, it now says so in plain words ("the browser holds an older copy of the data; reload without cache") instead of showing the raw error.

Not tested: in a browser with a deliberately stale cache. I reproduced the error's cause by reading the code, and I confirmed the current page loads with no error.

Turn 219

How do I check it on my phone, if its still in localhost?

Claude's response

Serve it on your local network and open it from your phone, as long as the phone is on the same Wi-Fi as your Mac.

Steps 1. In your own terminal (my sandbox can't open ports), from the project folder: python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 0.0.0.0 -d site/public Or type ! python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 0.0.0.0 -d site/public in the prompt here. 2. Find your Mac's address. This usually works for Wi-Fi: ipconfig getifaddr en0 If it prints nothing, use System Settings → Wi-Fi → Details → IP address. 3. On the phone, open http://<that address>:8000. For example, http://192.168.1.23:8000. 4. If macOS asks whether Python may accept incoming connections, choose Allow. 5. Stop the server with Ctrl-C when done.

If it won't load - Campus or office Wi-Fi often isolates devices from each other. A symptom is that the phone can't reach the Mac even on the same network. Switch both to your phone's hotspot, or connect the Mac to the hotspot, and use the Mac's new address. - The data files must be current. The server serves whatever is in site/public/data, which I re-exported, so that's fine. - Phone fonts need internet. The page fetches Google Fonts, so the phone needs a connection.

Two alternatives - Desktop approximation: in Chrome, open DevTools (Cmd+Option+I), toggle the device toolbar (Cmd+Shift+M), and pick a phone size such as 390px. It's quick but doesn't show real touch behaviour or real mobile font rendering. - After publishing: open the public GitHub Pages URL on the phone. That is the real test, and it's public by then. I'd avoid temporary tunnel tools like ngrok for this, because they expose your Mac's server to anyone with the link.

Tip: on the phone, check the explorer's two-judge blocks (they should stack), the overview's charts and the whitepaper's tables, since those are the parts most likely to overflow. If anything looks off, tell me which page and what you see.

~/Projects/Election-Promise-Tracking/docs/ui/design-brief.md
# Website UI/UX: design brief (branch `ui`)

Scope: `site/public/` presentation only. The pipeline, the exporter and `data/*.json` are untouched.
Needed exporter changes are listed in `docs/ui/exporter-requests.md`.

## 1. Diagnosis of the current site
- The overview shows ~10 blocks at equal weight: switch, 3 cards, 2 charts, a 6-column table, 3 assumption boxes, 2 trust cards, 3 amber notes. Nothing says what the answer is.
- Honesty is present but scattered: three yellow note boxes of different length compete with the data.
- Work done is invisible on the overview and over-detailed elsewhere.
- Controls and layout are styled inline (`style="..."` on the judge buttons), so they do not read as one system.
- The 390px layout loses the projection table (6 columns) and wraps chart legends badly.

## 2. Audience and the 60-second path
**Audience:** a course professor (Data Science & AI) who has 1–5 minutes, possibly a viva afterwards; secondarily a curious member of the public. Both need the answer and the caveat together.

# usage: docs/ui/shot.sh <page.html> <width> <outfile> [theme]

  timeout 90 "$CH" --headless=new --hide-scrollbars --virtual-time-budget=8000 --window-size=$((W>520?W:520)),$SL --screenshot="$D/s$i.png" "file://$D/w.html" >/dev/null 2>&1
done

I redesigned the overview, whitepaper, work and explorer pages on branch ui and committed them as 2666c67. python -m pytest -q passes (395 tests, exit 0). Nothing is pushed or published.

What changed

  • Direction: I proposed three (Briefing, Dashboard, Story) in docs/ui/design-brief.md and implemented A, "Briefing". The theme is CSS tokens only, so a different direction from Claude Design means editing :root and spacing, not the HTML.
  • Overview:
  • It now leads with a hero and the judge switch.
  • Three findings follow the switch: the completed terms' share realised, the TVK month-5 gap between judges (3.3% vs 22.9%), and the TVK projection range (19%–65%).
  • There is one chart per section.
  • The three projection lines are still there, each with its Assumes and Weakness.
  • The month table and "who judged what" now sit behind <details>.
  • There is one limits strip, and a small "Behind these numbers" strip linking to work.html.
  • Whitepaper: I added a summary box and a table of contents, and turned inline (1)–(5) enumerations into lists. Wording is otherwise kept.
  • Work page: Stages are now collapsible cards.
  • Explorer: It uses the same styling as the other pages, with the judge names spelled out.
  • Accessibility and layout:
  • Projection lines also differ by dash pattern, not colour alone.
  • Charts have text summaries for screen readers.
  • There is no horizontal scroll at 390px or 320px.
  • Light and dark both render.

Screenshots and docs

  • Screenshots: docs/ui/before/ and docs/ui/after/, at 1000px and 390px, with the overview also in dark. docs/ui/shot.sh regenerates them.
  • docs/STATUS.md: I added a separate "UI work" section at the end. It will probably conflict with the main conversation's own appends at the end of that file when you merge.

For the main conversation

  1. Exporter fields: docs/ui/exporter-requests.md lists what to add to work.json: spot-check counts, undated documents, memory probe, and retrieval row count. Pages already bind to those paths and show the old typed text until the fields exist. Console messages list the missing paths. Work-page stage 08 says "nothing on it is typed by hand", which isn't literally true until then.
  2. Whitepaper wording: docs/ui/whitepaper-changes.md lists every touched or new sentence.
  3. Section B: reworded sentences. The main ones are §5 split into several sentences, and the concordance in §10 now computed (0.56 and 0.57 instead of "about 0.56 in both").
  4. Section C: new sentences, which are the summary bullets and the overview findings. Each restates something already on the pages and is data-bound.
  5. Section D: text that is already stale (see below).
  6. D-120: When the Claude-only run lands, the "who judged what" texts in whitepaper §5 and on the overview will be out of date. A third judge setting would also need a third switch button and its own summary_*.json and model_*.json.
  7. Rounding: The Gemini-only agreement is 29/40 = 72.5%. The site shows 73% and D-119 says 72%. It's the same data, only a different rounding rule.

I didn't touch the exporter, data/*.json, or the uncommitted reports/runs/judge-*.json change, which belongs to the main conversation.

I did not use Google Forms' blue, green, orange and red, for two reasons: - Green, red and orange (red plus yellow) break your own rule about party colours and their mixes. - Colouring the terms red and green would read as party branding, which cuts against the site's "no party-coloured judgments" line. Colour-blind visitors also struggle to tell red from green.

That's why I used blue, violet and cyan. The lines also differ by dash pattern, so colour isn't the only cue. If you still want the Google-style set, it's a three-line token change. I'd keep it away from the terms and use it only where colour has no party meaning.

The new overview is built and committed on ui as 4e784a1. All 395 tests pass, and the only console message on the overview is the expected list of missing exporter fields. There is no horizontal scroll at 400px or 320px, and light and dark both work in purple and blue.

You can view it at http://localhost:8765/ (blue: ?palette=blue, dark: ?theme=dark).

What's on the overview, in the order from the brief

  1. Robust findings. Two panels, "Holds under both judges" and "Depends on the judge". Each claim is tested on the JSON before it's shown. If one stopped holding, say after the Claude-only run, it would move to the "depends" panel automatically.
  2. Gemini-only / Claude-only toggle. One toggle drives both the term cards and the Kaplan–Meier curves. Terms are compared with 100% stacked status bars, in a ramp of the accent colour plus greys, so nothing looks like party colours. There are no pies.
  3. One Cox forest plot. Two markers per characteristic: Gemini is a hollow circle and Claude a filled diamond, so the judge never depends on colour alone. A table sits behind a <details>.
  4. Pace strip. k with its 80% interval against 1.0, plus the documented month-5 shares of AIADMK, DMK and TVK under the same judge. The reading underneath says "roughly 81%–92%" because that's what pace.json gives, not the 80–90% in the brief.
  5. Two projection panels. Each shows "historical pace" and "if TVK's current pace persists", the second labelled an extrapolation, not validated as a forecast. Scenario A is gone from the overview. A note explains that the pace update helped only when the two terms had different judges.
  6. Accuracy against the 40 hand labels. Aggregate numbers only, with n = 40 and no TVK labels stated.
  7. Work done link band. It has a link and no figures.

Look: each section is a full-width band with its own gradient, and the data sits in glass panels. The TVK section is a dark band, like Apple's contrast bands. Anything Claude-only that comes from the stand-in carries a "preliminary" tag.

Whitepaper: it now has the like-for-like pace paragraph, the extrapolation caveat, and scenario A kept with its explanation. Scenario B keeps its "chosen after scenario A's result was seen" label, and the "most likely" wording is untouched.

Where to find things

  • Before/after screenshots at 1000px and 400px, light and dark, plus the blue version: docs/ui/v3/.
  • Every sentence that is new or whose meaning could have changed, for checking against the specs: docs/ui/whitepaper-changes.md, sections E–G.
  • Exporter changes the main conversation should make: docs/ui/exporter-requests.md §4. The main ones are a final_claude block in evaluation.json, an explicit TVK n of 0, and flipping meta.standin to false when the Claude-only run finishes.

Things to know

  • Shared folder. The main conversation's commits (1f61722, 5a00bf4) went onto ui, because we share one working folder and I switched it to ui earlier. The main branch is now behind ui and hasn't moved. Because ui contains everything on main, merging it into main is a plain fast-forward. Neither conversation should switch branches without telling the other.
  • Three judgement calls:
  • Toggle order: Gemini-only comes first and is the default, because it's the complete setting. The brief wrote Claude-only first.
  • "Side by side": I read it as both settings shown at once with no toggle. The forest plot and the TVK section each get their own full-width band.
  • Accuracy cards: The Claude card uses Claude's own raw verdicts until a Claude-only final exists in evaluation.json, and its caption says so.
  • Rounding. The Gemini-only agreement is 29/40 = 72.5%. The page shows 73% where the decision log says 72%.
  • Palette. Purple is still the default, and ?palette=blue is a remembered switch. Tell me which to keep and I'll remove the other.

The background color scheme is as follows: first hero one is fine, next can be pure white with text in dark purple/black, next can be black with white/light purple text, next light purple bg with black text and so on. I want to add more colours in the page in the progress bars, graphs, liquid glass panels(for contrast only). The party colour rule can broken but it should not be prominently so. Also, the % manifesto realisation - make it an animation when the user scroll reaches there. Reorganise it to stack the three terms vertically, make the bars longer and animated with more colours and place the labels on the right (similar to the hero part alignment). Graph, make it a contrast with the background. The highlights - % completion of manifesto and TVK projection must stand out from the rest. Otherwise overview looks good. The footer, put the disclaimer on top, leave a line or two and post the licensing. Remove the file name. Also why is a lot of the text only reaching 65% of the page width and then moving to the next linbe? Was this a design choice?

Claude's response

Before writing code, let me answer your last question: yes, the narrow text was a design choice, but I over-applied it. Capping line length at about 60–70 characters is a readability convention for long paragraphs, and I applied it to short intro lines too, where it just looks like wasted space. I'll widen it on the overview. I'll keep it for the whitepaper's long-form text unless you say otherwise.

All of that is done and committed on ui as 30f59f2. You can see it at http://localhost:8765/. The tests pass (395, exit 0), there's no horizontal scroll at 400px or 320px, and there are no console errors.

What changed

  • One look: Purple only. Dark mode and the blue palette are gone, along with ?theme and ?palette. All four pages are now a single mode.
  • Section order:
  • Completed terms
  • Promise characteristics
  • TVK pace and projection
  • Conclusions (the old robust findings, with the same two columns inside)
  • Accuracy
  • Work link
  • Backgrounds: Hero unchanged, then pure white (dark text), black (light text), light purple (black text), then white, black and light purple again. Each band has subtle gradient shading on top of that base.
  • Contrasting panels: Dark glass panels sit on white and lavender, and light glass panels sit on black. The forest plot is a light panel on the black band, and the KM chart and projections are dark panels on the light bands.
  • More colour:
  • Statuses: Cool colours (violet, blue, cyan) mean realised. Warm colours (gold, orange, pink) mean not realised. Grey stripes mean no evidence.
  • Terms: AIADMK is blue, DMK is orchid and TVK is cyan.
  • Judges: Gemini is orange and Claude is violet, in the forest plot, pace strip and accuracy cards.
  • Accuracy cards: They now have coloured meters, with a pale band for the 95% interval.
  • Gradient frames: The two headline sections get a multicolour gradient frame.
  • Manifesto realisation bars:
  • Layout: The three terms are stacked vertically, with long multicolour bars. The labels sit on the right, in the same alignment as the hero, with big term-coloured percentages.
  • Animation: The bars grow and the numbers count up when you scroll to them. When you flip the Gemini/Claude toggle they animate to the new values. Visitors who prefer reduced motion get the final state at once.
  • Headline sections: Term realisation and the TVK projection get a "Headline result" tag, much larger headings, and the multicolour frame. The projection panels show their month-60 numbers at 60px.
  • Footer: Disclaimer first, then a gap, then the course line and licence. The verdicts file name is removed, and the footer is now a full-width black band on every page.

The narrow text

It was a design choice, but I over-applied it. Capping a line at about 60–70 characters is a readability convention for long paragraphs, and I used it on short intro lines too. That left the text stopping at about 65% of the width. Intro text on the overview now uses the full width. The whitepaper's long-form paragraphs keep the narrow measure. Tell me if you want those wider too.

Your call

  • Warm colours: Gold, orange and pink sit in small segments, and the gold and orange are the most visible. They do touch party colours, though not prominently, as you allowed. Unverifiable is grey, not "not realised". The legend labels it "Not realised, or no evidence".
  • Screenshots: Before/after at 1000px and 400px are in docs/ui/v4/. There's no light/dark pair this time. shot.sh now forces reduced motion so the captures show the final state.
  • Ledger: The new wording is in docs/ui/whitepaper-changes.md. No whitepaper text changed this round.

Turn 232

I like this for the light theme, make dark theme also, but keep it colourful (My bad). Thinner bars and smaller digits for the headline promise. I thought the animation would start from 0% on the bar and move when the user reaches this part, but this only works while toggling, so change this. Could we also make the graphs start from origin and reach their final state via animation when the user reaches the respective parts? Animation for the recall as well. Wait, does this make it look like a glorified PPT?. The disclaimer - replace 'lang models' with LLMs.

f369503 site: dark theme, scroll-driven animations, explorer redesign with pagination, corrections section and moderated comments

Everything is done and committed on ui as f369503. The site is at http://localhost:8765/. I tested it in a real browser, and the tests pass (395, exit 0).

Overview changes

  • Dark theme: It's colourful, with purple-black bands, vivid bars and charts, and glass panels with coloured glows. It follows your OS setting until you press the moon/sun button in the header, then remembers your choice. ?theme=dark forces it.
  • Bars and digits:
  • The term bars are about 40% thinner.
  • The headline percentages are about 40% smaller.
  • Animation fix: The animation did work when I tested it in a real browser, but it started when only 30% of the section was visible. On a tall window that happens at page load, before you've scrolled anywhere.
  • It now starts only once the section is in the upper three quarters of the screen.
  • Every animated part resets when you scroll away, so it replays each time you arrive.
  • Graphs: These now play on arrival:
  • KM and projection charts: They grow up from the x-axis.
  • Forest plot: The markers fan out from 1.0.
  • Pace strip: The markers slide from 1.0 to k.
  • Accuracy meters: Recall and the other meters fill, and the percentages count up.
  • Reduced motion: Visitors who prefer reduced motion get the final state at once.
  • Footer: It now says "Verdicts are made by LLMs…".

Promise explorer

  • Hero: A big bold "Promise explorer" with the intro running the full width. The "No evidence found" note is now smaller and in red.
  • Results: 10 per page, which is the Google convention, with Previous, 1, 2, 3 … 168, Next.
  • Corrections: The corrections part is now its own section with a large heading, matching the overview sections. It has three numbered steps.
  • Comments: Another section, with a "Why this website exists" panel, a form, and the approved comments. That panel's wording is mine, summarising spec 08 §1. Please confirm it says what you want.

About the comment filter

This is a static site, so it can't store or screen anything on a server, and I won't pretend to filter hate automatically. What I built: 1. Browser check: The form checks length, links, caps and a short list of abusive words before anything is sent. That list is only a first pass and will miss things. 2. Public GitHub issue: The comment goes out as a public GitHub issue. The visitor needs a GitHub account, and their GitHub name is visible on the issue but never shown on the site. 3. You approve it: A comment appears only after you approve it by adding it to site/public/community/comments.json. The page re-checks that file against the word list before showing anything. The steps are in docs/ui/moderation.md.

A real automated filter would need a backend, which would end the "static site" rule in spec 08. I added a short "General comments" paragraph to whitepaper §12 describing exactly this.

Is it a glorified PPT?

Partly, yes. Full-width colour blocks, one big headline per section, "Headline result" badges, rainbow frames and entrance animations are all slide-deck habits. What stops it being a deck is the content: uncertainty bands, tables behind <details>, the explorer, the whitepaper and the stated limits. For a professor skimming in a minute the deck feel helps. For an evidence-first, neutrality-first project, motion and colour can read as selling. If you want to dial it back, I'd drop the rainbow frames and the "Headline result" badges first and keep the animation to the two headline sections. That's your call, so I haven't changed anything.

Needs the main conversation

  • The ledger of new wording is in docs/ui/whitepaper-changes.md, last section.
  • The exporter note for approved comments is in exporter-requests.md §5.
  • Before/after screenshots at 1000px and 400px, light and dark, are in docs/ui/v5/.

All of that is done and committed on ui as 5cb6139. The tests pass (395, exit 0), and there's no horizontal scroll at 400px or 320px. The site is at http://localhost:8765/.

What changed

  • Overview: The rainbow frames and "Headline result" badges are gone. The two headline sections keep their larger headings. The animations are untouched.
  • Explorer hero: The "1,674 promises" and "3 terms" counts are removed, and the hero is smaller. The headline is about 60px at most (it was 84px), and the padding is tighter. The intro still runs the full width, and the red note is still small. The promise count still appears in the results line.
  • Whitepaper and Work done: Both now open with a hero band like the others. I moved their existing title and intro paragraph into it at a larger font, with no new words. The whitepaper intro was small grey text before, so it's now much more prominent.
  • Whitepaper outline: The Tamil Nadu outline uses the same shape as the overview, shared from site.js. It sits fixed on the right and doesn't move while you scroll.
  • Tables over the outline: Tables are now opaque cards the colour of the page, so the outline disappears behind a table only where the table is. Nothing in the tables is cut. The tip of the outline peeks out above a table and comes back below it.
  • Narrow screens: The outline is hidden below 1080px wide, since the text would run into it.

The whitepaper now has a standard gap under "13. Reproducibility and licences". It's about 87px on desktop and 66px on a phone. This is committed as c6bd623, and I've stopped making UI changes.

Will running the remaining batches damage the UI?

No, the layout won't break. All numbers, charts and tables are drawn in the browser from the JSON files that python -m ept export-site writes. The batches themselves change nothing on the site until someone runs that export. After that, the pages pick up the new data on their own. Specifically: - Bars, curves, forest plot, pace strip, projections and accuracy meters all resize to whatever the new numbers are. - The "Conclusions" findings are tested against the data each time. A finding that stops holding moves to "Depends on the judge" instead of staying and becoming false. - "Preliminary" tags disappear once the exporter sets meta.standin to false in the Claude files. - A backtest month marked unavailable prints "not available in this setting".

What could go wrong, and the guard I added

The real risk is the export changing shape, for example a missing field or a renamed key. To catch that, I added tests/test_site_contract.py. It lists exactly what the pages read from the data. I checked it by damaging a copy of the data on purpose: it flagged both the removed projection band and the removed pace field. The real data passes. After you re-export, run python -m pytest -q. If it fails, the message names the field.

Things that will go stale, not break

These are hand-written texts. They won't crash, but they'll say the wrong thing once the results change: - The sentence describing what Claude judged, in whitepaper §5 and on the overview. - "Dates are approximate, by about five to six months". - "Claude is stricter… found fewer realised promises", the description of the Claude-only setting.

Re-read those three once the final numbers are in. They're listed in docs/ui/whitepaper-changes.md, section D.

Housekeeping

  • Re-export: After the batches finish, re-run export-site so the data files update.
  • Shared branch: Both conversations commit on ui, so you can merge ui into main with a simple fast-forward.
  • Server: The preview server is running again at http://localhost:8765/. If it stops, restart it with python3 -m http.server 8765 -d site/public.
